events.title: An Evening of Scottish Fiddle
about: An Evening of Scottish Fiddle; featuring Isabel Oliart & Kyra Davies with Eamon Sefton on guitar Tickets: $20 in advance, $25 at door, $15 for seniors This concert is part of the Trad on the Mystic organized by Ellery Klein and hosted at Arts Collaborative Medford Isabel Oliart is a Boston-based fiddler spanning the the worlds of Classical and Celtic fiddle music. She earned a BA from New England Conservatory in 2019, and an MA in Violin Performance from Boston University in 2024, where she also won the Bach Competition.

She won the 2025 National Scottish Fiddle Championship, and has been a first-place winner of the New Hampshire Highland Games Fiddle Competition (2023), and the Scottish F.I.R.E. Composition Competition (2021). Isabel’s music has been featured on GBH’s A Celtic Sojourn and on NPR’s Says You. She has released two albums: ‘Late Evening’s Dram’ and ‘Tartan Rants and Rhapsodies’. She has performed at the Rockport Celtic Festival, Groton Hill Music Center, BCM fest, the Burren, Club Passim, the Loon Mountain Highland Games, and numerous other venues across New England. She was also part of the Boston Philharmonic Orchestra for many years and has subbed with the Albany Symphony and the New World Symphony Orchestra.

Kyra Davies is a Boston-based violinist and fiddler whose multilayered performance career has taken her from San Diego, California to Siena, Italy. She can be found performing in arenas, concert halls, intimate house venues, or circus tents, with artists including The Who and the Eagles, symphony orchestras, chamber ensembles, and bands. Kyra specializes in contemporary music and has premiered dozens of pieces, both as a chamber musician and with the Boston Modern Orchestra Project.

In 2025, Kyra was crowned the New England Regional Open Scottish Fiddle Champion. With her duo project Mrs. Wilberforce and other groups, she has performed music from Scotland, Ireland, and other Celtic-influenced traditions at venues around New England. She regularly accompanies Scottish country dances and leads Scottish and Irish sessions.

events.title: The Jam Down By Riverside (potluck)
about: The Jam Down By Riverside is a direct descendant of the now defunct Blues Jam at the Porch Southern Fare & Juke Joint, which was a descendant of the Johnny D’s blues jam. The jam is for building community and building skills. We welcome people of all ages, abilities, styles and instruments to join in the jamming. We do not have a strict Blues Only jam rule, but probably 85% of the repertoire is blues or blues-derived music. Please come to play or listen.
The jams are on the Second Sundays of the month from 1-4pm.
We’re putting out a special call to teachers and their students to join us and we’re specifically trying to facilitate connections between people with more experience and folks with less experience.

The Jam is first come – first served, meaning you get into the pool to play when you arrive and sign up. There will be 3-4 different groups per hour depending on attendance. More people = shorter sets and more sets, so more people are able to play. The host will put different bands together based on the abilities and instrumentation available from the attendees. Each group will have a bandleader (often the lead vocalist) who will call songs, solos, starts, breaks and endings.
This is a potluck event, so bring food to share or bring you own eats. We will have beverages for sale for your convenience.
Please Do bring your own instrument, cable, sticks, microphone, and small harp amps.
Please Do not bring your own guitar amp and unless you have talked to the host in advance.

Volunteers will provide the following backline for players: drumkit, bass rig, 2 guitar amps, 2 direct boxes, microphones, monitors, PA system. We are taking donations of various equipment for backline. Please inquire about a donation. In particular we are looking for a small drumset and <15w guitar amps or modeling pedals.
We will ask for donations to offset the cost of the event and to show support for our organization.

about: The Beantown Buckaroos cook up classic Western Swing and Country music, with a dash of Tex-Mex and Cajun for picante. You could say we play both kinds of music, Country and Western.

The Bucks were born when a few vets of Boston’s roots community got to powwow with some cowboys new to town, all of us steeped in the music of the great American Southwest, from Bob Wills, Merle Travis, and vintage honky-tonk, to contemporaries like Doug Sahm, Asleep at the Wheel, and The Hot Club of Cowtown.

about: John Doyle and Mick McAuley’s nearly telepathic musical connection began in the truly groundbreaking Irish-American band, Solas. For over thirty-five years, including multiple studio recordings, musical collaborations, and awards, Cathie Ryan has been in the vanguard of Irish music. Now, these three luminaries of Irish music come together to celebrate the Christmas and winter holidays with an evening of exquisite traditional and contemporary songs, tunes, and stories fitting of the season. From familiar carols to special ones that are less well known, as well as new material and their own personal holiday stories, An Irish Christmas with John Doyle, Cathie Ryan and Mick McAuley is a beautiful and evocative evening from these three stellar artists.

John Doyle’s influences include well-known English folk singers Nic Jones, Martin Carthy, Richard Thompson and The Watersons; Scottish singers Dick Gaughan and John Martin; fellow Irishmen Paul Brady and Al O’Donnell; and his father, Sean Doyle—probably the biggest influence of all. Having started his professional career at the age of 16, John went on to form the highly acclaimed supergroup, Solas, with Seamus Egan, John Williams, Karan Casey and Winifred Horan, which took the folk and Celtic music worlds by storm, in no small part due to John’s powerhouse rhythmic guitar style and innovative arrangements. Since then, John’s flourishing solo career, highly regarded solo albums, and in-demand studio prowess as producer have made him one of the busiest artists in all of traditional music. He is a Grammy-nominated artist for his 2009 recording with fiddler Liz Carroll, “Double Play”, has performed at the White House, was music director for folk music legend Joan Baez, guitarist for Mary Chapin Carpenter, and has recorded and/or performed with a who’s who of folk, Celtic, bluegrass and old-time music, including Tim O’Brien, Kate Rusby, Eileen Ivers, Karan Casey, Rodney Crowell and Jerry Douglas. John’s original rhythmic and percussive guitar style has been emulated by guitarists all over the world.

Cathie Ryan has built a loyal following by touring internationally and singing “songs of the heart” at performing arts centers, festivals, folk clubs, and with symphony orchestras. Cathie is a captivating performer whose shows are renowned for their intimacy and power – and a typically Irish sprinkling of storytelling. “There…

events.title: Holiday Concert Benefitting Foster Love
about: Tonight, Jamie Dunphy & True North celebrate the release of their new holiday 7-inch, A Post-Punk Christmas Card, featuring the original single “Give Me Something Good for Christmas.” The band features three seasoned musicians with a long history in the Boston music scene: Jamie Dunphy (The Beige, Mill City Trio), Seth Peterson (Electric Standard, The Gone Boys, Capital 6) and Tod Salmonson (The Snap Daddies, Dr. Smigley's Baby). The trio formed in 2018 and have been performing regularly since at Boston-area venues including the Burren Backroom, the Midway Cafe, Lilypad Inman and the Square Root. In May 2025, the band released Stage Dive Into Oblivion, a collection of four singles including The Last Song, 1983, Everything Must Go, and Snowfall, which Stereo Stickman called "a gorgeously refreshing classic."
"A superbly crafted pop-rock CD" -Roots Music Report.
"A gorgeously enjoyable, interesting and professionally crafted album from a band with a timeless authenticity to their sound." -Stereo Stickman.
"A perfect album for our times." -Metronome Magazine.
"The band combines expert musicianship with a folk singer's style and a keen appreciation for the hook." -The Static Dive.

Spawned in the cellars, garages and clubs of Western MA’s Pioneer Valley, the Bamboo Steamers have been playing high energy roots rock and roll for several decades. The band recently re-released their acclaimed debut album, The Many Love Making Sounds of the Bamboo Steamers, and are currently playing is support of their most recent EP, Six Minutes to Everything. The Daily Hampshire Gazette said of the group, “their original music is timeless, combining surf/spy instrumentals (a la The Ventures, Shadowy Men on a Shadowy Planet, Los Straitjackets) and vocal songs that bounce with a spry, countrified gait.”

events.title: Hilary Hawke Band, Stash Wyslouch
about: The Hilary Hawke Band is a fun, powerhouse quartet featuring guitarist Ross Martin (Jacob Joliff Band, Matt Flinner Trio), fiddler Camille Howes, and bassist Myles Sloniker (Jacob Joliff Band) based out of NYC. Since forming as a trio in 2022, the group has built its identity around improvisation, original songwriting, and a shared love of bluegrass and old-time traditions. Hilary and Ross bring over 15 years of shared musical history across a range of bluegrass projects while also stretching into the world of original music. The band leans into songwriting and improvisation, with performances that are vibrant and engaging. Expect banjo drive, soaring fiddle melodies, intricate guitar work, tasteful bass lines, rich harmonies, all grounded in songs that celebrate creativity, and the joy of being live in a room with an audience.

Stash Wyslouch - Guitarist Stash Wyslouch is hailed as one of bluegrass’s most powerful genre‑bending pioneers—a firebrand whose “sonic kaleidoscope of weirdness and wonder” mixes thrash metal, old‑time, jazz, and classic bluegrass into wildly original, jaw‑dropping music that somehow feels both delightfully zany and deeply soulful.

Stash has played and recorded with Bruce Molsky’s Mountain Drifters, The Jacob Jolliff Band and The Deadly Gentlemen and shared the stage with the likes of Bryan Sutton, Billy Strings, Julian Lage, David Grisman and Peter Rowan.

events.title: Jay Bragg Presents: Christmas in New Vaudeville
about: From Nashville, Jay Bragg's beloved "Christmas in New Vaudeville" returns to The Burren in Somerville, MA bringing The Merriest Show On Earth — now in its 6th annual year — to his home base of New England. Jay, whose grandparents performed in 1930s vaudeville, transforms into bandleader King Kazoo from the North Pole, adorned in his signature bright red frock coat, top hat, brass kazoo, and a dose of whimsy that only the Wizard of Whimsy can muster — leading The Reindeer Band through a joyful, theatrical night of original and holiday music built for the whole family. Equal parts vaudeville throwback and Christmas spectacle, this is a holiday show like you've never experienced and will never forget.

events.title: The Nightflies
about: New selections, first-time by us, from Gaucho, The Nightfly, The Royal Scam, Katy Lied..and more.

A 10-piece band from the Boston/Merrimack Valley area that began as an informal get-together, for the love and challenge of playing the intricate arrangements of Donald Fagen and Walter Becker. Our name is a tip-of-the-hat to the 1982 standard-bearer Donald Fagen solo album,The Nightfly.

The Nightflies perform an ambitious medley of those recognizable, danceable, foot-tapping, 70's-80's hits and plenty of Becker/Fagen's deep-cuts. Hear faves from...Can't Buy a Thrill, Countdown To Ecstasy, Pretzel Logic, Katy Lied, The Royal Scam, Aja, Gaucho, and last but not least Fagen's solo effort, The Nightfly. The Nightflies are available for venues, private parties, and corporate events.

events.title: Matt Heaton’s Burren Boogie - Family Music Sundays Holiday Edition
about: Matt Heaton’s fun for the whole family kids show residency continues!

Matt Heaton believes music for kids can be entertaining for both children AND parents. His songs blend mid century American guitar styles: surf, rockabilly, western swing & soul, delivered with a wry sense of humor and a sincere sense of fun. Children and adults respond to his musicianship and variety. The grown ups in the room particularly appreciate the Muppet-esque touches of humor and observations of kid behavior. Whether you call it children's music, family music, kindie or toddlerbilly it's sure to please listeners of all ages.

events.title: Torch Light Music School
about: Welcome to Torch Light Music School's 25th Anniversary Show!! Featuring our finest soloists, groups and songwriters from our new SongWrite Class! We're so excited...come celebrate!!

events.title: Tiger Moan First Sunday Blues
about: Amy Kucharik and Tiger Moan invite special guests each month and push the tables aside to make room for dancing.

Tiger Moan: Specializing in vintage blues with sass and class, Tiger Moan is in the fifth year of their residency playing first Sundays every month at the Burren Backroom. Tiger Moan has entertained blues and swing dancers at events such as Sweet Molasses Blues, Blues Union, Yale Swing & Blues and MIT's Bread & Bones fusion dance. The band is known for covering the best blues standards and for funky originals with innovative lyrics.
VIDEO: com/24hourconcerts/videos/475070391026184

events.title: Brian O’Donovan Legacy Series: Coig Christmas
about: Celebrate the season in style with one of Atlantic Canada’s premiere Celtic supergroups as they take concert goers on a musical journey with their renditions of timeless Christmas classics, brimming instrumentals and high-energy original tunes. An exceptional show from start to finish, Còig brings various influences to their Celtic holiday mix ranging from Folk, Classical, to Swing, giving your favourite carols a fresh and original sound. The quartet features four accomplished multi-instrumentalists and award-winning musicians, Rachel Davis, Darren McMullen, Margie Beaton and Thierry Clouette.

events.title: Fletcheros
about: Fletcheros is the long running cover band based out of the Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy at Tufts, proving that diplomacy nerds can also rock out. From Ariana Grande to Nirvana to The Police, they play it all. Members may be transient, but Fletcheros transcends the test of time.
fletcheros.cover.band/

events.title: Invisible Sun - Featuring The Music of The Police
about: Invisible Sun started 15 years ago when Scott Babineau, Brian Chaffee, and Chris Reddy decided to play some songs by The Police at a jam session. That session turned into an annual event and with the addition last year of drummer Rick Dondero, Invisible Sun has become one of the premier Police cover bands around. They cover 25 songs from The Police, spanning all of their recorded work, with special attention to the detail and stylings of the originals!
Brian Chaffee is an accomplished vocalist/keyboardist from the Gardner area who has fronted "The Franks," "Krakow" and now regularly performs with “Hot Mess”!
Scott Babineau is a fixture in the central Ma music scene as a solo artist, front man for the very popular "Caves on Mars" and session/live work with multiple area musicians, including Mark Marquis.

Chris Reddy, besides being a solo artist performing “Acoustic Loops from Hell," is currently working as the lead guitar player for the band "Doctor Robert" and was the lead singer/ lead guitarist for the Prog rock band "Transit" for 25 years. He has opened for Dave Mason, Gary Hoey, Stan Ridgeway, Jim Weider and Johnny A.

Rick Dondero, who has been playing drums for over 3 decades, has taken the reins as drummer for Invisible Sun. He also plays with Scott in “Caves on Mars” and is currently playing with several other central Ma. bands, as well. An accomplished drummer, Rick pays attention to the essence of Copeland’s ska and jazz elements.
If you enjoy the music of The Police, you must see this show!
Invisible Sun: Brian Chaffee (lead vocals/keyboards) Scott Babineau (bass/lead Vocals) Chris Reddy (lead guitar) Rick Dondero (Drums/Percussion)!

events.title: Opera Untapped : Drunk Opera History: Messiah Sing
about: Join Opera Untapped as we turn the New England Messiah Sing tradition on its head, adding the fun back story about Handel, a little trivia, and a casual atmosphere where you can sing along… with a beer in hand if that’s your vibe. Expect epic vocal soloists, hilarious anecdotes, and a joyful sprinkling of trumpet to tie it all together. By the end of this family-friendly afternoon, we'll have the whole crowd on their feet for a raucous Hallelujah Chorus!

Opera Untapped brings people together through bold, intimate, and innovative performances that showcase the beauty, drama, and humanity of the classical voice. Through immersive productions, interdisciplinary collaborations, and community-centered programming, Opera Untapped creates joyful artistic experiences that surprise, inspire, and connect audiences of all backgrounds. Learn more at

events.title: New England Irish Harp Orchestra - NEIHO
about: The New England Irish Harp Orchestra has been delighting audiences for twenty six years. The Orchestra consists of many harpers, hailing from the New England states, along with fiddle, bodhran, and voices. They have toured in the States and Ireland and have produced four CD’s.
$25 in advance. (+ processing fees) $30 at the door.
This Is An All Ages Show Doors are at 6pm. Showtime is 7pm. Dinner and drinks available at all tables.

events.title: All That Music Academy - Winter Showcase!
about: All That Music Academy is home to musicians of all ages and skill levels and we are so excited to host our annual Winter Showcase at The Burren! You will hear all genres of music from classical, to pop, rock, r&b and even metal! Our musicians range from ages 4.5 to over 80 and may have started taking lessons a few months ago, or started taking lessons many years ago. This show is open to all ages and we invite friends and families to join us for a great day of performances.

events.title: JGB Tribute, The Diamond Blues
about: Diamond Blues, delivers high-energy, soulful, and exploratory performances in tribute to the one-of-a-kind, rock-gospel-soul-rhythm and blues group, Jerry Garcia Band.
Since 2021, Diamond Blues, an eclectic group of accomplished musicians passionate about honoring the legacy of Jerry Garcia, have taken New England by storm.

Led by David Rubin on Vocals & Guitar, Diamond Blues features Robbie Parrish on Drums, Ian Brenkle on Bass, Caroline Killoh on Vocals & Keys, and Christopher Belden on Sax and backing vocals. An ensemble capable of furnishing any era of the Jerry Garcia Band story.

DB, as it’s often called by fans, mines their repertoire from the Jerry Garcia Band songbook and blends other fan favorites consistent with the original sound of JGB. Their uniquely crafted setlists touch the entire catalogs of JGB, Legion of Mary/Merl Saunders, and Jerry Garcia Solo, leaving audiences inspired and electrified. DB blends deep cuts with hits that will have you respectfully asking, “why didn’t Jerry play that more often?”
$17 in advance. $22 at the door.
This Is An All Ages Show Doors are at 7:30. Showtime is 8pm. Dinner and drinks available at all tables.

events.title: Which Side?: A Protest Music Teach-Out
about: Which Side?: A Protest Music Teach-Out is a concert and discussion series celebrating and exploring protest music.

The events uses James Sullivan’s book, Which Side Are You On?: 20th Century American History in 100 Protest Songs, as a starting point for the presentation of songs that ask listeners to consider how music gives voice to resistance, advocacy, and change. While the series will anchor itself to the book, collaborators will also contribute 21st-century music, both originals and covers.
The show is scheduled to begin promptly at 8 p.m.
Admission is pay-what-you-want, with all proceeds going to the musicians and other direct expenses.
Tickets can be reserved, but a reservation does not guarantee entry unless you are in the room by 7:30 p.m.
If there are people waiting for entry, reservations will be released starting at that time.
This series is produced by Joyce Linehan, Jon Lupfer, and James Sullivan, with the help of many generous friends.
Nov 17th features Kevin Connolly, Nicolas Emden, Grace Givertz, Kay Hanley, Lenny Lashley, and CA McNeill Dec 15th features Maverick, Surya Gopal, Brian King, Vance Gilbert, Hilken Mancini, and more.
They will be backed by the Which Side house band, The Paid Protesters. The 90-minute show will also feature commentary by various interesting people.
Admission is pay-what-you-want, with all proceeds going to the musicians and other direct expenses. Please keep this in mind while picking a price.
Thanks to those who always pay a little bit more, so those who can’t afford as much can have access as well. Your generosity is very much appreciated.

IMPORTANT: Your purchase is a RESERVATION, and a reservation does not guarantee entry unless you are in the room by 7:30 p.m. If there are people waiting for entry, reservations will be released starting at that time, and money will not be refunded.

events.title: Brian O'Donovan Legacy Series: Lúnasa’s “Irish Solstice Celebration” with special guest singer Dave Curley - TWO SHOWS
about: One of the most influential bands in the history of Irish traditional music, celebrated its twenty fifth anniversary in 2022. Named after an ancient Celtic harvest festival in honour of the Irish god Lugh, the group that Folk Roots magazine once called an “Irish music dream team” was formed from members of some of Ireland’s greatest bands and over the years has proven its mettle time and again, having sold over a quarter of a million records, performed more than 2,000 shows in high-profile concert venues across 36 countries, and collaborated with many notable artists outside the tradition. Two decades ago they ascended to the forefront of contemporary Irish music, and there they’ve remained, a leading voice in the genre and the standard against which others are compared.
“…state-of-the-art Irish music as aggressively infectious as you’ll ever hear.”
– Dirty Linen (2000)
With special guest singer Dave Curley!

events.title: Brendan Cleary + Wilf: Album Release Show
about: In 2019, Brendan Cleary’s life restarted. After years of struggling with addiction, the world came crashing down. It was the beginning of the road back to finding his voice again.

Playing hotel bars and restaurants, Brendan slowly felt his way back to the songwriter he had always been at heart, connecting with audiences through stories of his struggles and victories. His hard work paid off: Brendan has since been named a finalist in the New Hampshire Music Collective Songwriting Competition, has appeared on NHPR’s The Folk Show with Kate McNally, WSCA’s The Button Factory Soundcheck, and Maine Public Television’s 207 to discuss his story and music. In 2025, Folk legend Tom Rush invited Brendan to tour across the United States as his accompanist.

This December, Brendan releases his debut studio record, Soundbox: an intimate portrait of a songwriter rediscovering his voice through failure, love, and recovery. He joins Wilf at The Burren for a year-end release show celebrating two voices from Cambridge’s songwriting scene.

Wilf is a Boston-based singer-songwriter whose introspective music blends droning indie folk with traditional ballads. Often using alternate tunings, his songs carry an ominous quality that, paired with poetic lyrics, attempt to transfer personal ruminations onto the audience for self-reflection. His debut EP, Pity, releases November 13, 2026, and draws inspiration from artists including Ethel Cain, Elliott Smith, and Slowdive. The EP dissects the transition into adulthood, examining feelings of stagnation and self-pity.

events.title: Evan Goodrow
about: Join the group in celebrating their 19th record "Time in Time Out" with Jake Walters on keys and Fabio Pirozzolo on percussion.

Evan Goodrow is an American singer-songwriter-guitarist who has written and produced 18 recordings of original soul, funk, blues and rock music. He’s won the Boston Blues Award, played concerts for Marines on Nato bases in Europe, charted in Amazon's top 10 indie artists, but most importantly had a beer named after him from the BackBeat Brewery.

events.title: Teen Battle of the Bands
about: Don't miss the Teen Battle of the Bands featuring local up-and-coming young rockers from Medford, Arlington, and Winchester. The show will include some original songs as well as covers spanning classic rock, grunge, and indie rock.

events.title: The Nervous Eaters with Special Guest Geoff Abraham Band
about: The Nervous Eaters are an original rock and roll band from Boston, MA who helped define the Boston underground garage/punk rock scene of the late 70’s.
Geoff Abraham Band delivers high-energy bluesy rock 'n' roll with infectious hooks, unforgettable melodies, and plenty of swagger..
$25 in advance. $30 at the door.
This Is An All Ages Show Doors are at 6pm. Showtime is 6:30pm.

events.title: A Charlie Brown Christmas
about: Come experience the magic of the season as a live jazz piano trio brings A Charlie Brown Christmas to life on stage! This heartwarming performance captures the nostalgic charm of Vince Guaraldi’s iconic soundtrack, featuring beloved tunes like “Linus and Lucy,” “Christmas Time Is Here,” and more. Performed with improvised, authentic arrangements and the warm energy of live musicianship, this show is a joyful celebration for all ages—perfect for fans of Snoopy, jazz lovers, and anyone who wants to embrace the holiday spirit. Bring your friends and family for an unforgettable day of timeless music and festive cheer!

events.title: A Very FUNdraising Xmas
about: Boston’s ’90s band Fuzzy started a rock ’n’ roll Xmas tradition back in the early ’90s that has continued every year since. More than 30 years later, A Very FUNdraising Xmas remains one of Boston’s most beloved holiday shows, bringing together the city’s favorite rock musicians for an unforgettable evening of holiday songs, community, and cheer — all to benefit Rosie’s Place! Part concert, part reunion, and all heart, this annual celebration features live music, raffles, prizes, giveaways, and MCs Gene Dante, Angelle Wood, and Andrea Gillis. The all-star lineup includes Muck and the Mires // Merrie Amsterburg // Jen Trynin // Magen Tracy // David & Stephen Fredette // Hilken and Melissa Band // Chris Colbourn // The Handymen // Drew O’Doherty & Family // Other Girls // Thalia Zedek // Mike Gent, plus members of Buffalo Tom, Scruffy the Cat, and more! Come celebrate over three decades of Boston’s favorite rock ’n’ roll holiday tradition!

events.title: Adina, Aphrodite, Cyanide
about: Adina is a vocalist and guitarist that has performed at several different local venues. Sydney (Bass) and Noah, (Drums) have played at several different venues, with the punk rock band, Split Lips.
Cyanide is a high school band consisting of 3 musicians. We typically do rock/metal covers, and are currently expanding to originals.
Aphrodite is a punk/riot grrl Burlington, bringing wonderful noise to you.

events.title: Double Barrell, Mill Street
about: DOUBLE BARREL plays great rock and pop covers, from the past to present with a hard rock edge. An experienced local band that has been on the scene for over 30 years. Playing a variety tunes from past to current pop tunes. The band features Aaron Lewis (not of stained) on drums and some lead vocals / back round vocals. Mark Lewis (lead/ rhythm guitar). Gary Moulter (Bass). Eric Sowyrda (rhythm/lead guitar). Gabe Smith(Lead Vocals).

MILL STREET is a group of veteran Boston musicians that are also good friends. They play a broad range of country and rock covers. Think from JJ Cale, Linda Ronstadt and the Mavericks, and then all way to Ace and the Beatles. The band features Pete MacDonald (vocal, guitar), Norm MacDonald (guitar), Carrie Martin (Keyboard, vocals), Amy Cain (Vocals), Sheldon Mirowitz (guitar), Josh Hassol (Bass) and David Morse (drums).

about: Matt Heaton’s fun for the whole family kids show residency continues!

Matt Heaton believes music for kids can be entertaining for both children AND parents. His songs blend mid century American guitar styles: surf, rockabilly, western swing & soul, delivered with a wry sense of humor and a sincere sense of fun. Children and adults respond to his musicianship and variety. The grown ups in the room particularly appreciate the Muppet-esque touches of humor and observations of kid behavior. Whether you call it children's music, family music, kindie or toddlerbilly it's sure to please listeners of all ages.

events.title: Brian O’Donovan Legacy Series: Rockaway Bound
about: Rockaway Bound is a new project led by award-winning Irish accordion player Diarmuid Ó Meachair, inspired by the vibrant Irish music scene that flourished on New York’s Rockaway Peninsula during the 1920s and 1930s. Legendary musicians including the McNulty Family, Peter Conlon, Michael Coleman, Paddy Killoran and John McKenna performed in Rockaway during the summer months, helping shape the distinctive sound of Irish music in America’s golden gramophone era. Rockaway Bound aims to capture the spirit, energy and creativity of this period while bringing its legacy into the present day. The band’s first run of shows will take place in January 2027, Diarmuid will be joined by some of the most exciting young musicians in Irish traditional music: Seamus Noonan (flute), Andrew Caden (fiddle), Colman Connolly (piano) and Richard Osban (Greek bouzouki).

events.title: Yani Batteau
about: Yani's clawhammer style banjo picking and rootsy vocals enhance her soulful new arrangements of her original music. She invites you on a journey of love, redemption and the everyday experiences that we all live.

events.title: School Of Rock Medford - Adult Showcase
about: School of Rock is not just for kids!

Our Adult Program is ready to take the stage with two powerhouse sets featuring an eclectic mix of artists, from Led Zeppelin, Fleetwood Mac, and Radiohead to System of a Down, Blondie, and more. Spanning decades and genres, these sets bring together everything from hard-hitting rock anthems to alternative favorites and classic hits. Come cheer them on and see just how hard the adults can rock!

events.title: The Honey Steelers Brunch!
about: The Honey Steelers are a Lowell-based Americana band playing original tunes and reimagined covers from artists like Asleep at the Wheel, Ray Charles, John Prine, Lucinda Williams, Bob Dylan, and The Beatles. Their blend of cowboy swing, country rock, folk, and blues features sweet harmonies, rotating vocals, and solos on pedal steel, mandolin, guitar, and keys. They'll have you stomping your feet one moment and humming a lullaby the next—often while laughing at their on stage banter. Smart, soulful, and just a bit goofy. Fun for all ages!

events.title: Frank Viele w/Special Guests Liz Reed & Bri Green
about: Frank Viele’s brand of New England blues rock tugs at the heartstrings, pulling the listener on a surprise journey that transcends genre. The Silo EP, being released on Frank’s own Bigger Beast records (a label started to support and highlight some of Frank’s favorite artists, collaborators, and friends), serves as the next step in this artist’s journey. Over the past decade, Frank has racked up accolades — including New England Music Awards for Independent Artist of the Year, Album of the Year, Song of the Year, Male Performer of the Year, Songwriter of The Year (twice), and Live Act of The Year for gutsy, gritty tracks like “Broken Love Song” and “‘Til The Bourbon’s All Gone” — and he has rarely paused to savor the moment before moving on to yet another tour, album, or collaboration. It wasn’t until the pandemic hit in early 2020 and he was forced to hunker down that Viele realized that time itself was the world’s most precarious, yet precious, resource.

Viele’s music is characterized not only by his powerful vocals, soulful guitar playing, and poignant lyrics, but also its deep honesty, and this EP is no different. "After opening for Lee DeWyze on over 100 shows across 10 years, I had the opportunity to collaborate with him and his long-time producer Nico on this project, bringing a deep connection and understanding to the production process,” Viele says.

Liz Reed - With the easygoing warmth of Jim Croce and the everyday storytelling sensibility of John Prine, Liz Reed makes music that feels like pulling up a chair at the kitchen table with somebody who understands exactly what kind of day you’ve had.
A mother of two, public school music teacher, activist, and community builder, Liz has spent much of her life helping other people find their voices.
And somewhere between raising a family, teaching children, and showing up for her community, she’s found a pretty remarkable way of sharing her own.
In 2025, Liz was nominated for Songwriter of the Year by the New England Music Awards. In 2026, she was a finalist in the Songwriting competition of the South Florida Folk Festival.

Liz's Bigger Beast Records singles, “Maybe Kind of World” and “The Human Side,” explore the little contradictions of being human. The struggle to remain compassionate when the world makes it difficult. The courage it takes to keep showing up. The realization that kindness isn’t always the…

events.title: Avanza, FM Collective
about: Avanza is a globally inspired band that is making a unique splash in the Boston music scene by introducing audiences to world musical stylings and international cultural influences they could never find. Our approach is to take contemporary pop and infuse it with traditional musical influences from Spain, Latin America, and all over the world. We sing in multiple languages, including English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, Arabic, Hindi, and more! We do this so as many people as possible can see themselves represented and share in our music. Our goal is to make a change in the Boston music scene by getting more people to fall in love with Spanish, Latin, and world music and bring people of all backgrounds together to hear a part of their identity represented in a way that everyone will love.

FM Collective is an award-winning Boston-based band blending Latin rhythms, jazz, funk, and contemporary influences into an energetic, danceable live experience. Winners of the 2025 New England Music Award for World Act of the Year, the group has performed over 200 shows across New England and beyond, bringing audiences together through original music, infectious grooves, and a multicultural sound.

events.title: Brian O'Donovan Legacy Series: Karan Casey TWO NIGHTS
about: Irish singer-songwriter Karan Casey has been blazing a trail for over 25 years. A lover of ballads, love songs and searing versions of social justice songs, she has toured extensively throughout North America, Europe and Japan, performing with her own band as well as collaborating with such diverse musicians as Maura O’Connell, James Taylor, Bela Fleck, Boston Pops Orchestra, The Chieftains, The Dubliners, Peggy Seeger, Karen Matheson, Mick Flannery, Mícheál Ó Súilleabháin and Tim O’Brien.
In 2018 Karan helped to found FairPlé which is an organization aimed at achieving fairness and gender balance for female performers in Irish traditional and folk musics.

Her album Hieroglyphs That Tell the Tale is on the Vertical Records Label. Her song “Down in the Glen” was nominated for Best Original Folk Song at the RTE Folk Awards 2019 and she completed a PhD in music in 2019. Her last highly-acclaimed album, Nine Apples of Gold, was released February 2023 to great acclaim, holding the number one spot on the International Folk Charts for all of March 2023, with 8 of the songs from the album in the top 20 spots.

events.title: Chinese Americans in Science & Technology
about: MIT-China presents the China Diaologue Series. Panelists Professors Xiaoxing Xi and Gang Chen, moderated by Professor Yasheng Huang, will explore how professional achievement can intersect with heightened national-security considerations. Drawing on personal experiences and institutional perspectives, the discussion will address evolving policies and the broader implications for academia, scientific research, and international collaboration.

events.title: SURGE: A Participatory Performance on Sea Level Rise
about: Experience sea level rise through this interactive performance-workshop that combines movement, climate science, and activism at the MIT Museum.

Choreographer Jessie Jeanne Stinnett and Boston Dance Theater Core Members will lead a 45-minute participatory workshop. Through guided movement and collective exploration, you'll engage with sea level rise impacts—ocean warming, ice melt, tidal dynamics, and shifting coastlines—and contribute your own perspectives as the workshop builds toward imagining possible futures. No dance experience is needed.
A 30-minute performance follows, where audiences mingle with performers to witness, reflect, and dialogue about climate science and coastal change.
SURGE creates an accessible space for curiosity, conversation, and collective understanding of climate challenges, where science, art, and community voices intersect.
We have a limited number of free tickets available for full-time students with ID. Please reach out to museumregadmin@mit.edu.
This program is presented as part of the MIT Museum’s thematic focus on OCEANS.

events.title: Graduate Student Talk: Tony Chen
about: Join Tony Chen, a PhD student at MIT’s Brain and Cognitive Sciences for a conversation around Hao Jingban: I Witness.

How might our bodies help us think? In this talk, Tony will discuss what cognitive science can tell us about the ways physical actions change what we perceive, remember, and reason about. He will ask how far this relationship between action and understanding extends to our emotional lives, drawing on the practice of Authentic Movement explored in Hao Jingban’s film, I Witness, to better understand how movement might help people make sense of their grief and loss.
This event is free, but please register through the Eventbrite link in advance.

Tony Chen is a fifth-year PhD candidate in MIT's Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences, where he studies the computational basis of human problem solving and planning. His research asks how people can solve complex problems in mathematics, science, and everyday life despite limits on their time and memory. He approaches this question through a combination of behavioral experiments, computational modeling, and large-scale online data analysis.

MIT graduate students explore current exhibitions at the List Center through the lens of their own research, background, and interests. Join us for this interdisciplinary lecture series where we dive into how art and research are overlapping on MIT’s campus.

events.title: Author Ted Chiang in Conversation with MIT President Sally Kornbluth
about: Join us for a special conversation with author Ted Chiang and MIT President Sally Kornbluth about Exhalation. President Kornbluth has chosen Chiang’s celebrated science fiction short story collection to celebrate 10 years of MIT Reads. Exploring the book’s provocative questions about technology and humanity, their discussion will focus on the stories "The Truth of Fact, the Truth of Feeling,” "The Lifecycle of Software Objects,” “Omphalos,” “What’s Expected of Us," and "Exhalation."

In this fantastical and elegant collection, Chiang wrestles with the oldest questions on Earth – What is the nature of the universe? What does it mean to be human? – and ones that no one else has even imagined. And, each in its own way, the stories prove that complex and thoughtful science fiction can rise to new heights of beauty, meaning, and compassion.

This event is part of MIT Reads, a program that embraces the power of reading and storytelling to cultivate social connection, individual reflection, and a sense of our shared humanity. Designed to foster empathy, curiosity, and belonging, MIT Reads brings together the campus community – and readers everywhere – through common reading experiences, author talks, and group discussions.

events.title: AI and the Future of Filmmaking
about: W97-160 · December 3 · Lecture and Discussion – 6-7.30p

AI and the Future of Filmmaking What works, what doesn't, and what comes next AI can now generate convincing video from a sentence. But can a filmmaker actually direct it? William Cusick, filmmaker and former Creative Director at Stability AI, has been making films with generative AI and building tools for it since the launch of Stable Diffusion in 2022. In this talk he shows what AI filmmaking can do today, where it breaks down, and what it changes about cameras, sets, actors, and the director's job. He places the moment in a century of film technology, then looks ahead to real-time AI worlds where a film is generated while you watch it.
45-minute talk followed by discussion.
RSVP please. Open to all; no technical background needed.

William Cusick is a New York filmmaker and creative technologist who specializes in AI filmmaking. He was Creative Director at Stability AI during the public launch of Stable Diffusion and DreamStudio, and he is building Moviengine, an experimental system that turns screenplays into AI-generated films. He has directed two feature films, including Welcome to Nowhere (Bullet Hole Road) and Pop Meets the Void, designed projections for Broadway and international stage productions, and has taught at The New School for more than thirteen years.

events.title: Meriem Chabani. Communion It is embarrassing to believe. It is terrifying to care. What happens when we dare anyway?
about: Algerian born, Paris based Meriem Chabani is the founder and Principal of NEW SOUTH, an award-winning architecture, urban planning and anthropology practice that puts the margin at the center. Her work on civic spaces, memory and belonging includes the Taungdwingyi cultural center in Myanmar, the Globe Aroma refugee art center in Brussels, and the upcoming Mosque Zero in Paris. She is currently a finalist for the National Slavery Museum in Amsterdam. As an educator, Chabani has taught and lectured extensively. She has notably served as Aga Khan Design Critic in Architecture at Harvard GSD (USA), and currently teaches at Ecole Paris Malaquais (FR). Her work has regularly been distinguished and showcased at a number of international architecture Biennials, including Venice, Istanbul, Oslo and Lagos. In 2020 Chabani won the Europe 40 under 40 award from The European Centre for Architecture and The Chicago Athenaeum. In 2023, she is one of the emerging women architects for AMC. In 2025, Le Monde names her one of the leading voices in culture in France.

Sacred practices are often confined to religion, yet they can also be read as technologies of togetherness, ways of gathering bodies, knowledge, and memory into forms of collective action that outlast the institutions built to contain them.

Drawing on recent work by NEW SOUTH, this lecture explores how rituals, communal practices, and sacred spaces may shape architecture. From shared acts of making and gathering to spaces shaped by migration, displacement, and diasporic memory, these projects ask how architecture can support forms of solidarity that aren't always visible or formally recognized. Ritual here is also a spatial claim, a way of reoccupying ground for those pushed to the margins, relegated out of the mainstream, and denied formal recognition.

The lecture will explore how rituals rooted in care for land and its resources may offer a different model for building — one grounded in reciprocity rather than extraction. Architecture becomes less an object that organizes people than a framework through which people organize themselves. We may yet belong. We may yet forge futures not built on depletion.
Photo: Religious and Cultural Center in central Paris

events.title: Author Talk: Paul Lewis — Quothing "The Raven"
about: Boston College Professor Emeritus Paul Lewis leads a discussion of his new book, Quothing "The Raven": The First Responses to America's Most Famous Poem.

In 1845, over 5,300 poems were published in American magazines. Most immediately began their deserved descent into oblivion. Poe's "The Raven" stands as the most conspicuous exception to this. But why? What factors influenced the attention devoted to "The Raven" from the day when it was first published? Why was it widely reprinted, praised, criticized, and mocked during the next weeks and months? Why did it inspire parodies that replaced Poe's "saintly bird of yore" with a veritable menagerie of other animals—including an owl, gazelle, turkey, pig, dog, cats, rats, and (eek!) bedbugs? And how did Poe's reputation—as a literary brawler and harsh book reviewer and as a man who struggled with money and alcohol—play into the reception of "The Raven"?
Signed copies of Paul Lewis' Quothing "The Raven": The First Responses to America's Most Famous Poem will be available at this book-launch event.

Paul Lewis is a Professor Emeritus at Boston College, a past president of the Poe Studies Association, and the curator of exhibitions on literary Boston. As the Board of Directors chair of the Edgar Allan Poe Foundation of Boston, Inc., Lewis worked with others to celebrate Poe in the city of his birth by having a square at the intersection of Boylston Street and Charles Street South dedicated to Poe in 2010 and then installing a statue of Poe in it in 2014.

events.title: Author Talk: Steven Levitsky — How Democracies Die
about: Author Steven Levitsky discusses his New York Times bestselling nonfiction book, How Democracies Die.

The United States’ descent into competitive authoritarianism during the second Trump presidency should never have happened. No democracy even remotely as rich or as old as America’s has ever broken down. American society had more than enough muscle to thwart an authoritarian offensive. But political, business, and civic leaders either acquiesced to the Trump administration’s authoritarian bullying or quietly stepped to the sidelines, allowing Trump’s authoritarian offensive to accelerate. This talk asks why U.S. elites abdicated in the face of an authoritarian threat, explores the prospects for reversing the authoritarian turn, and discusses what we can do to prevent it from happening again.

Steven Levitsky is David Rockefeller Professor of Latin American Studies and Professor of Government and Director of the David Rockefeller Center for Latin American Studies at Harvard. His research focuses on democratization and authoritarianism, political parties, and weak and informal institutions, with a focus on Latin America. He is co-author (with Daniel Ziblatt) of How Democracies Die, which was a New York Times Best-Seller and was published in 30 languages, and Tyranny of the Minority: Why American Democracy Reached the Breaking Point. He has written or edited eleven other books, including Transforming Labor-Based Parties in Latin America: Argentine Peronism in Comparative Perspective (Cambridge University Press 2003), Competitive Authoritarianism: Hybrid Regimes after the Cold War (with Lucan Way) (Cambridge University Press, 2010), and Revolution and Dictatorship: The Violent Origins of Durable Authoritarianism (with Lucan Way) (Princeton University Press, 2022). He is currently writing two books: one on the crisis of American democracy and another on global democratic resilience. Professor Levitsky is a Senior Fellow at the Kettering Foundation. In 2026, he was elected to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. Professor Levitsky has written for New York Times, The Washington Post, The Atlantic, Foreign Affairs, and The New Republic, and he has been a columnist for La Republica in Peru.

events.title: Author Talk: Cotten Seiler on “White Care”
about: Join Dickinson College professor Cotten Seiler for a conversation about his new book, White Care. The book discusses how few of us, going about our daily lives, notice the infrastructure that surrounds us and makes those lives possible. What also remains hidden in plain sight is how public infrastructure in the United States has been shaped by theories of race and human evolution. Cotten Seiler’s White Care shows that, from the late 1800s to the present, expert assessments of the quality of the national population have both driven and thwarted the state’s provision of infrastructures of water, sanitation, energy, transportation, recreation, and education. If a nation’s infrastructure is a concrete measure of its belief in its population’s future, what does the current state of American infrastructure say about us?

Cotten Seiler is a professor of American Studies at Dickinson College whose work focuses on U.S. cultural and intellectual history, race, feminist and political theory, and infrastructure humanities. He is the author of the books Republic of Drivers: A Cultural History of Automobility in America (Chicago, 2008) and White Care: The Impact of Race on American Infrastructure (Chicago, 2026), coeditor of Engaging Mobilities: Interventions in Pedagogy and Practice (Berghahn, forthcoming 2027), and editor-in-chief of Transfers: Interdisciplinary Journal of Mobility Studies. His essays have appeared in journals such as American Quarterly, Public Culture, Social Text, Reviews in American History, and History & Technology. He is a frequent media commentator on US politics, automobility, race, and infrastructure and can be reached at In discussion with Seiler is Dr. Karilyn Crockett. Crockett's research focuses on large-scale land use changes in twentieth century American cities and examines the social and geographic implications of structural poverty, racial formations and memory. Her book, People before Highways: Boston Activists, Urban Planners, and a New Movement for City Making (UMass Press 2018) investigates a 1960s era grassroots movement to halt urban extension of the U.S. interstate highway system and the geographic and political changes in Boston that resulted. about: This exhibit by Laura Gatzos, contains depictions of familiar and comforting scenes and places we encounter as New Englanders. Artist Statement: I create art that is detailed, yet calm, brightly colored, yet gentle. In a world that encourages cynicism, sarcasm, and hard edges, my art offers an alternate proposition where kindness is valued, and the restorative properties of the natural world can offer a soothing respite.

I draw and paint the places where I find calm: my family farm and environs in Vermont, where I grew up and return to as often as I can; the Emerald Necklase and conservation lands in the Boston area, where I go when I need an escape; Greece, the homeland of my husband's family, where I am in awe of the beauty of the land, the architecture, and the sea.

Bio: Laura Gatzos has been creating art for as long as she can remember, using pastels, oils, watercolors, and acrylics. Born and raised on a dairy farm in the Northeast Kingdom of Vermont, Laura is inspired by nature and seeks to capture the beauty and restorative properties of the natural world.

Professionally, Laura combines creativity and her love of science, technology, and her previous experience as a medical technologist to support research computing endeavors at the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, finding solutions which promote cost-savings, increase computing efficiency, and improve ease-of-use for members of the DFCI research community.

events.title: The Inevitable Return: Exploding Plastic Revisited
about: On October 29, 1966, the ICA/Boston hosted a groundbreaking multimedia performance by Andy Warhol and the Velvet Underground under the enigmatic title “Exploding Plastic Inevitable.” Presented as part of Warhol’s second-ever museum exhibition, the event invited audiences to experience a cacophony of durational light and sound activations, meant to challenge any expectations of instant pleasure or gratification. The Velvet Underground had become well-known for their dark, minimalist, and occasionally abrasive sound. Among Warhol’s goals for the piece were to explore the capacity to bestow renewed interest upon details that are often submerged in the normative, evenly lit flow of time. In addition to live music, the night consisted of film projections, a variety of strobe and spotlights, and choreographed dance, to create a singular, and confrontational, total-art experience.

On the occasion of “Exploding Plastic Inevitable’s” 60th anniversary and as part of 90 YEARS, the museum’s deep dive into its long and storied history, the ICA resurrects the spirit of what has been called one of the greatest concerts in Boston history. The December 11 event will feature performances and installations by Boston Cream, Caleb Hawkins, The Croaks, Cursed Image, DakouDakou, Organs Studios, Pleasure Coffin, System Failure, and The Dregs Liquid Light Show.

events.title: Andrew Schneider: NOWISWHENWEARE (the stars)
about: Every point in space occurs once at each moment in time.

NOWISWHENWEARE (the stars) makes that literal. Inspired in part by Yayoi Kusama’s Infinity Rooms, the stars moves beyond an immersive gallery experience: an unseen narrator guides each visitor through an individualized journey into a matrix of light, of the cosmos, and of the self.
Open Universe: $20 ICA members / $25 students / $30 non-members, Guided: $30 ICA members / $35 students / $40 non-members

events.title: Ogemdi Ude: MAJOR
about: MAJOR is a dance theater project exploring the physicality, history, sociopolitics, and interiority of majorette dance, a form that originated in the American South within Historically Black Colleges and Universities in the 1960s. These Black femme teams accompanied by marching bands created a movement style that requires master showmanship with allegiance to count, undulation, groove, and sensual yet strong performativity.

In MAJOR, six Black femmes embrace majorette form – a fundamental relic of Black girlhood – to pursue the intimate journey of returning to bodies they thought lost. Experiments in improvised and verbatim language intertwine with a music score that integrates Southern rap, horns, drumlines, and melodic R&B and soul by Lambkin. A fierce investigation of physical memory and community, MAJOR is a nuanced love letter to the folks who taught the team how to be proudly Black and proudly femme.

events.title: Dune: Part Three
about: From Warner Bros. Pictures and Legendary Pictures comes Dune: Part Three, bringing Academy Award-nominated filmmaker Denis Villeneuve’s epic trilogy to a breathtaking conclusion.

Dune: Part Three is set nearly two decades after Paul Atreides seized control of the Imperium. Now a ruthless Emperor, Paul must face the consequences of his reign as old allies return, terrifying new threats emerge, and betrayal lurks in every shadow. Haunted by visions of Imperial collapse and the reappearance of his long-lost love, Paul is drawn into a sweeping conspiracy, with Chani at the heart of its unfolding mystery. As rebellion brews and enemies close in, Paul must confront the true cost of power and the fate of those he loves the most.

The film stars Oscar nominee Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya, Jason Momoa, Oscar nominee Florence Pugh, Rebecca Ferguson, Isaach de Bankolé, with Oscar nominee Charlotte Rampling, with Anya Taylor-Joy, and Robert Pattinson, and Oscar winner Javier Bardem.

Villeneuve directs from a screenplay by Villeneuve and Brian K. Vaughan, based on the novels written by Frank Herbert. The film is produced by Oscar nominees Mary Parent, Cale Boyter, Villeneuve and Tanya Lapointe, and Joe Caracciolo, and executive produced by Joshua Grode, Thomas Tull, Herbert W. Gains, Brian Herbert, Byron Merritt, Kim Herbert, Kevin J. Anderson, Richard P. Rubinstein, John Harrison and Jessica Derhammer.

Joining Villeneuve behind the camera are Oscar-winning director of photography Linus Sandgren, Oscar-winning production designer Patrice Vermette, Oscar-winning editor Joe Walker, Oscar nominated costume designer Jacqueline West, Oscar-nominated casting director Francine Maisler, and Oscar-winning composer Hans Zimmer.

Warner Bros. Pictures and Legendary Pictures Present A Legendary Pictures Production, A Film By Denis Villeneuve, Dune: Part Three, only in cinemas December 17, 2026. The film will be distributed worldwide by Warner Bros. Pictures and in China by Legendary East.
Directed by Denis Villeneuve · 2h 25m

events.title: White Christmas
about: Join West Newton Cinema for a musical matinee! Our monthly pick will vary from beloved classics to jazz, from vaudeville to psychedelic rock, brought to you by the imaginative skill of artists able to make scenes look the way great music feels. We’ll feature films from the Golden Age of Hollywood musicals, with surprises that transcend the era and define others. The cinematic brilliance of these films has never left us. In fact, seeing them again, or for the first time, will reinvigorate your love for the movie musical and send you out of the theater tapping your feet.

With its timeless Irving Berlin musical numbers—including its iconic title track—White Christmas is a holiday classic for a reason. In scenes shimmering with superstar performances, we watch as Bing Crosby and Danny Kaye join forces, dancingly and romantically, with sister-act Rosemary Clooney and Vera-Ellen to save a struggling Vermont ski-resort owned by Dean Jagger’s retired Major General. Directed by Hollywood vet Michael Curtiz (Casablanca, The Adventures of Robin Hood), White Christmas is chock-full of memorable moments and infectious tunes, wrapping the holiday season into one perfect Hollywood package that’s sure to put anyone in the Christmas spirit.

events.title: Local Spotlight: Cut To David
about: Join us for a one-day only community screening of Cut to David followed by a post-film discussion with the filmmaker Sandy Jaffe and family, and other participants in the film.

David’s story is beautifully layered from the start: An adopted, Chinese-American, transgender teen, raised in a Jewish home in Boston with a filmmaker for a mom, with a camera always close by. As David journeys from high school to college to adulthood, Sandy Jaffe’s camera documents her family’s evolving relationship as each participant has a turn steering the narrative. Blending vérité footage, home videos, and candid conversations, the film begins as an effort to understand David’s gender transition and expands into a deeper exploration of identity, agency, authorship, power, and the complicated yet loving bond between a mother and her son. An intimate, fly-on-the-wall documentary, CUT TO DAVID considers the possibilities—and perils—of living visibly and openly, exploring how ethnicity, gender, religion, and parenting shape who we become.

Sandy Jaffe is a filmmaker and writer, and has taught screenwriting at various institutions in the Boston area. Her first documentary feature, Our Mockingbird, was a part of the PBS series America Reframed. She is a co-facilitator of a parent support group through Greater Boston PFLAG. Cut to David, her second feature documentary, premiered to a sold out audience at GlobeDocs 2026.

Jay Blitzman is a former public defender who specialized in representing youth and late teens. He served for 24 years as a juvenile court judge, retiring as the First Justice of the Middlesex Division of the MA Juvenile Court. He teaches law, consults on youth and criminal issues, and advocates for supporting youth voice and agency in all contexts.

David Blitzman graduated Magna Cum Laude from Ithaca College in 2020. He received his MSW in 2025 from Smith College School of Social Work, and works as a therapist in Greater Boston. David also volunteers for organizations which promote community engagement and collaboration.
1h 10m

events.title: Minotaur
about: Intrigue, corruption, betrayal, survival: the walls of the maze are closing in.
The latest from Academy Award® nominated writer-director Andrey Zvyagintsev (Loveless, Leviathan), Cannes Grand Prix winner MINOTAUR is a twist-laden parable for our times.

Russia, 2022. Amidst the comfortable trappings of affluence and domesticity, corporate executive Gleb (Dmitriy Mazurov) finds himself under siege on all fronts. At home, he is haunted by suspicions that his increasingly distant wife Galina (Iris Lebedeva) is unfaithful. At work, he contends with a demand from local authorities to draft a quota of employees for the war in Ukraine. Desperate to keep his hands clean, Gleb struggles to reassert control even as the collapse of his carefully ordered life seems fated to accelerate toward violence.

A pressure cooker in cinematic form, MINOTAUR uncovers and indicts the heart of societal darkness with searing clarity. Uniting intimately-drawn performances and stark visual power, this is peerless work from an indisputable master.
Directed by Andrey Zviaguintsev, Andrey Zvyagintsev · 2h 15m

events.title: Yury Butusov's "King Lear"
about: Presented in Russian with English subtitles RUNTIME: 3 hours 34 minutes (Includes a 10 minute intermission)

Yury Butusov’s visionary production shifts focus away from political tyranny to examine the agonizing collapse of generational bonds. On Maxim Obrezkov's barren stage hangs a massive, swaying moon as the world tilts off its axis. Artur Ivanov portrays a physically imposing Lear trapped between life and death from the start, unraveling alongside Victor Dobronravov’s Gloucester and Sergei Volkov’s cynical Edmund. Evgenia Kregzhde doubles magnificently as both Cordelia and the Fool. Driven by a sweeping, thunderous soundtrack, this interpretation turns the tragedy into a visceral, intense nightmare about human loneliness.

Yury Butusov (1961–2025) was one of the most influential and innovative theatre directors of his generation. Renowned for his emotionally charged visual language, bold reinterpretations of classical texts, and fearless experimentation, Butusov profoundly influenced contemporary European theatre. After leaving Russia in 2022, he continued to create productions across Europe until his death in August of 2025.

Directed by Fawn Veerasunthorn and Jason Hand, co-directed by Josie Trinidad and produced by Roy Conli, Disney’s “Hexed” opens exclusively in theaters November 25, 2026.
Directed by Fawn Veerasunthorn, Jason Hand, Josie Trinidad · 1h 49m

events.title: All of a Sudden
about: Marie-Lou Fontaine, director of a nursing home in the Paris suburbs, defies convention by adopting the ‘Humanitude’ method despite her team’s resistance. Her encounter with Mari Morisaki, a terminally ill Japanese playwright, transforms her life. Together, they turn the facility into a symbol of resistance and humanity against the system’s limits.
Directed by Ryûsuke Hamaguchi · 3h 16m

events.title: Wild Horse Nine
about: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris and Lee are dispatched from Santiago to Easter Island by their bureau chief, MJ. Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways.

events.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
about: Harry Lehman is an aging pickpocket who plies his trade with ever-diminishing returns in a drastically changed New York. Wallets stuffed with cash have been replaced by easily cancelled credit cards, and Harry struggles to make ends meet as he cares for his disabled wife, Rosie. When he unwittingly purloins and fences a valuable USB stick, Harry finds himself in a race against time to return the loot or face the rage of a vengeful crime family.

events.title: DAKHABRAKHA
about: Global Arts Live presents DAKHABRAKHA Drones, beats, and towering black lamb’s-wool hats all serve as a striking backdrop to the Ukrainian folk-rock quartet DakhaBrakha. With one foot in the urban avant-garde and the other rooted in Ukrainian village culture, the group’s self-proclaimed “ethno-chaos” is a refreshingly novel vision of Eastern European roots music. events.title: Hexed
about: An impulsive and unconventional teenage girl named Billie discovers secret magical abilities which, once unleashed, hurtle her into a spectacle-filled journey out of suburbia and into a vast witch realm called Hexe. Forced to team up with her cautious mother, Alice, they uncover family mysteries that could change the world of witches forever.

events.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping
about: Return to the world of Panem 24 years before the events of the original The Hunger Games, starting on the morning of the reaping of the 50th Hunger Games. The story chronicles the youth and origins of Haymitch Abernathy as he navigates the deadly arena under the peak of President Snow’s tyrannical reign

events.title: I Play Rocky
about: The electrifying true story about an unknown actor with an unshakable belief that he wasn’t just meant to write Rocky-he was meant to be Rocky Balboa. Told “no” at every turn, Sylvester Stallone bets everything on himself, holding the line on playing the lead against seemingly impossible odds.

events.title: Elf
about: One Christmas Eve a long time ago, a baby crawled into Santa's bag of toys... Raised as an elf, Buddy (Will Ferrell) grows into an adult three times larger than the biggest elf—and realizes that he will never truly fit in at the North Pole. This holiday season, Buddy goes looking for his true place in the world—in New York City. Buddy finds his workaholic father (James Caan)—who's on Santa's "naughty" list, a new mother (Mary Steenburgen) and a 10-year-old brother who doesn't believe in Santa Claus or elves. Here, now, Buddy discovers his destiny—to save Christmas for New York and the world!​

events.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping
about: From acclaimed director Francis Lawrence, THE HUNGER GAMES: SUNRISE ON THE REAPING follows sixteen-year-old Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) from District 12, beginning on the morning of the reaping for the 50th Annual Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell, the biggest Games yet with twice as many tributes.

Set in the world of Panem 24 years before the events of The Hunger Games, the story follows Haymitch into the arena, where he forms an unlikely alliance with fellow tribute Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace) and joins a coalition determined to challenge the Capitol’s control under President Snow (Ralph Fiennes). As the competition unfolds, Haymitch risks everything to take down the Games from within the arena — setting in motion the rebellion that will change Panem forever.
2h 38m

events.title: The Metropolitan Opera: Samson et Dalila (2026)
about: Sacred, scandalous, and irresistibly alluring, Saint-Saëns’s spectacular take on the biblical hero of legendary strength and the seductive Philistine whose beauty overpowers him returns in the Met’s larger-than-life production. Featuring a massive orchestra and chorus and some of opera’s most spellbinding tunes, this masterpiece of French grand opera is a feast for the eyes and ears, with an electrifying cast led by the formidable star pairing of mezzo-soprano Aigul Akhmetshina and tenor Clay Hilley, who makes a notable company debut.
3h 54m

events.title: The Metropolitan Opera: The Magic Flute Holiday Encore (2026)
about: The Met made history in December 2006 when it presented its first Live in HD transmission to cinemas worldwide: the abridged English-language version of Mozart’s The Magic Flute. Julie Taymor’s whimsical production features a winning ensemble—including tenor Matthew Polenzani, baritone Nathan Gunn, and bass René Pape—and returns to select movie theaters for a special encore presentation during the holiday season.
1h 56m

events.title: 14th
about: Written in the wreckage of the Civil War, the 14th Amendment was meant to close the door on the hierarchy of human worth. Instead, it has become a permanent argument. Ava DuVernay’s 14th pulls this constitutional fight out of the footnotes and into the present, chronicling the vicious battle over the amendment that has raged for over 150 years. Threading deep archival scholarship with piercing headlines of today, 14th brings together legal minds, politicians, historians and cultural voices in direct conversation with a question America still hasn’t settled: Who gets to belong?
1h 40m

events.title: The Royal Ballet - The Nutcracker (2025)
about: At a cosy Christmas party, young Clara meets the mysterious magician Drosselmeyer, who gives her a nutcracker doll. When the guests have departed and the house is asleep, Clara sneaks downstairs in search of the doll. Instead, she finds Drosselmeyer, who whisks her away on a journey into a whole world of enchantment: fantastical landscapes of flurried snow and glittering confection where toys come alive and the magic never stops.

Recorded live at the Royal Opera House in 2025, Peter Wright’s production of this festive family favourite sparkles to the wondrous swell of Tchaikovsky’s orchestral score, alongside the glow and grandeur of Julia Trevelyan Oman’s period designs.
2h 10m
