events.title: Sammy Rae & The Friends - the GET DOWN!
about: Go put a smile on somebody’s face, go tell somebody they’ve got a place in this world, go tell somebody you wanna be friends with them.

For as much as Sammy Rae & The Friends may be a band, this collective of dreamers and artists considers themselves a family first. That all-for-one and one-for-all camaraderie ignites their unforgettable and can’t-miss live shows, which serve as a catharsis for both the musicians and their fervent audience. Fronted by singer/songwriter Sammy Rae and honed through years of touring, the group is capable of flourishing in any spotlight thanks to its signature blend of palpable chemistry, deft virtuosity, and vocal fireworks.

Their sound, which has attracted new fans by the thousands in the past few years, is a unique mélange of Sammy’s influences: classic rock, folk and funk and sprinkled with soul and jazz. Rae has been building toward this moment since moving to NYC from Connecticut in her early 20s. Finding herself without a built-in peer group, she simply built it herself: the literal and proverbial Friends. When she started playing shows, she made sure the audience was part of the family too. Everything that’s happened since – from EP’s “The Good Life” (2018) and “Let’s Throw a Party” (2021) to sold-out shows in major markets and secondary markets alike across North American and the UK & Europe, to high-profile festival sets around the world, including Bonnaroo’s main stage, Sound on Sound, All Things Go, and more – has been based on friends telling friends.

After the release of their debut album “Something For Everybody” in 2024, Sammy Rae & The Friends have come to represent more than just a band: they are a full-on movement being adopted with refreshingly diverse clientele. Sammy Rae and the Friends new singles “You Just Wanna Get With My Friend” and “Boogie All By Yourself”, and “Sleep On My Couch” are out now!

events.title: Hexed
about: In Walt Disney Animation Studios' all-new magical coming-of-age saga, “Hexed,” an impulsive and unconventional teenage girl named Billie (voice of Hailee Steinfeld) discovers secret magical abilities which, once unleashed, hurtle her into a spectacle-filled journey out of suburbia and into a vast witch realm called Hexe. Forced to team up with her cautious mother, Alice (voice of Rashida Jones), they uncover family mysteries that could change the world of witches forever. Directed by Fawn Veerasunthorn and Jason Hand, co-directed by Josie Trinidad and produced by Roy Conli, Disney’s “Hexed” opens exclusively in theaters November 25, 2026.
1 hr 49 mins · PG

events.title: Hexed
about: In Walt Disney Animation Studios' all-new magical coming-of-age saga, “Hexed,” an impulsive and unconventional teenage girl named Billie (voice of Hailee Steinfeld) discovers secret magical abilities which, once unleashed, hurtle her into a spectacle-filled journey out of suburbia and into a vast witch realm called Hexe. Forced to team up with her cautious mother, Alice (voice of Rashida Jones), they uncover family mysteries that could change the world of witches forever. Directed by Fawn Veerasunthorn and Jason Hand, co-directed by Josie Trinidad and produced by Roy Conli, Disney’s “Hexed” opens exclusively in theaters November 25, 2026.

events.title: The Metropolitan Opera: Samson et Dalila (2026)
about: Sacred, scandalous, and irresistibly alluring, Saint-Saëns’s spectacular take on the biblical hero of legendary strength and the seductive Philistine whose beauty overpowers him returns in the Met’s larger-than-life production. Featuring a massive orchestra and chorus and some of opera’s most spellbinding tunes, this masterpiece of French grand opera is a feast for the eyes and ears. Giacomo Sagripanti conducts an electrifying cast led by the formidable star pairing of mezzo-soprano Aigul Akhmetshina and tenor Clay Hilley, transmitted live to cinemas worldwide.
3 hrs 54 mins

events.title: A Colonial Candlelight Concert
events.detail: The Light Before Christmas with Trek Track Collective
about: Based in the Berkshires, Trek Track Collective is a premier string quartet featuring violinists Eileen Markland and Hannah Roberts, violist Bing Liu, and cellist Robbie Wilson. Each musician brings a distinguished career spanning classical, jazz and folk traditions, creating a rich and expressive sound that is both elegant and deeply moving.

events.title: Albany Berkshire Ballet Presents: The Nutcracker
about: Celebrate the magic of the holiday season as Albany Berkshire Ballet (ABB) returns with its annual tour of The Nutcracker. Choreographed by ABB’s Artistic Director Madeline Cantarella Culpo, this beloved production features lavish sets and scenery by Stockbridge native and renowned theatre and film set designer Carl Sprague, with costumes by Sam Meredith. Young local dance students join professional ABB dancers in special children’s roles, sharing the stage with a company of performers from across the United States and around the world.

events.title: Rock the Halls: A Rock & Roll Christmas
about: From the producers of Moondance and Takin' It to the Streets comes Rock the Halls: A Rock & Roll Christmas—a high-energy holiday celebration featuring rock-inspired arrangements of beloved holiday classics, performed by an all-star band of Berkshire musicians

events.title: Rev Tor’s 15th Annual Dead Of Winter Jam Featuring Dead Man’s Waltz & Friends
about: Drawing from the Northeast festival scene, Dead Man’s Waltz brings seasoned musicians together for an adventurous trip through the Grateful Dead’s expansive songbook. Familiar melodies leave room for unexpected turns as the band follows the music wherever it leads. It’s a spirited celebration of songs built to be explored, shared and heard anew.

events.title: Magic Tree House: The Knight at Dawn KIDS
about: Fresh from their adventure with the dinosaurs, Jack and Annie return to the magic tree house and open a book about the Middle Ages. When Annie wishes she could visit the castle on its pages, the siblings are whisked back to the age of knights. Curious about the mysterious Black Knight and his quest, they set off through a castle full of surprises, from a grand medieval feast to secret tunnels and dancing suits of armor. As they search for a way home, Jack and Annie discover the power of hope and what it really means to be brave.

events.title: Moondance
about: From the feel-good charm of “Brown Eyed Girl” to the soulful pull of “Into the Mystic,” Van Morrison’s songs have a way of staying with you. Moondance brings that extraordinary catalog to the stage in a tribute concert celebrating the unmistakable sound and spirit of Van the Man.

events.title: Maria Mazzotta
about: Maria Mazzotta builds on a foundation of traditional music of her native Apulia, adding influences from southern Europe and north Africa and layering on fuzzy post-rock experimentation.

events.title: Yamato, The Drummers of Japan World Tour 2027 Tamayura: Echoes of the Soul
about: Yamato has been a leading force in Japanese taiko drumming for more than three decades. The troupe's performances combine masterful musicianship, athleticism, and visual spectacle.

events.title: Mary Prescott
about: Mary Prescott is a Thai American interdisciplinary artist, composer, and pianist. She will develop a new work during residency with the UMass Fine Arts Center, and will premiere the piece at this event.

events.title: Philadanco
about: Featuring a new work by hip-hop and street dance legend Rennie Harris!

events.title: An Evening with Tom Rush
events.detail: Accompanied by Matt Nakoa and Brendan Cleary
about: Tom Rush is a gifted musician and performer, whose shows offer a musical celebration…a journey into the tradition and spectrum of what music has been, can be, and will become. His distinctive guitar style, wry humour and warm, expressive voice have made him both a legend and a lure to audiences around the world. His shows are filled with the rib-aching laughter of terrific story-telling, the sweet melancholy of ballads and the passion of gritty blues.

Rush’s impact on the American music scene has been profound. He helped shape the folk revival in the ’60s and the renaissance of the ’80s and ’90s, his music having left its stamp on generations of artists. James Taylor told Rolling Stone, “Tom was not only one of my early heroes, but also one of my main influences.” Country music star Garth Brooks has credited Rush with being one of his top five musical influences. Rush has long championed emerging artists. His early recordings introduced the world to the work of Joni Mitchell, Jackson Browne and James Taylor, and in more recent years his Club 47® concerts have brought artists such as Nanci Griffith and Shawn Colvin to wider audiences when they were just beginning to build their own reputations.

Tom Rush began his musical career in the early ’60s playing the Boston-area clubs while a Harvard student. The Club 47 was the flagship of the coffee house fleet, and he was soon holding down a weekly spot there, learning from the legendary artists who came to play, honing his skills and growing into his talent. He had released two albums by the time he graduated.

Rush displayed then, as he does today, an uncanny knack for finding wonderful songs, and writing his own – many of which have become classics re-interpreted by new generations. (It is a testimony to the universality of his appeal that his songs have been folk hits, country hits, heavy metal and rap hits.) Signed by Elektra in 1965, Rush made three albums for them, culminating in The Circle Game, which, according to Rolling Stone, ushered in the singer/songwriter era.

In the early ’70s, folk turned to folk-rock, and Rush, ever adaptable, saw more room to stretch out. Recording now for Columbia, he toured tirelessly with a five-man band, playing concerts across the country. Endless promotional tours, interviews, television appearances, and recording sessions added up to five very successful but exhausting years,…

events.title: Bombyx Brass Collective: Music for a Festive Season
about: Celebrate the season with the Bombyx Brass Collective, under the direction of Juli Sansoucy and John Power, and 35 outstanding brass musicians and percussionists in an evening of brilliant brass music, operatic drama, traditional favorites, and festive holiday sounds!

The concert's featured work is Giacomo Puccini's Music from Tosca, arranged by Geoffrey Boyd. Experience the sweeping melodies and dramatic intensity of one of opera's most beloved composers, brought to life through the rich, powerful sound of a large brass ensemble.

The program spans a remarkable variety of musical styles. Josef Suk's stirring Fanfare from "Towards a New Life" and Percy Grainger's spirited Duke of Marlborough showcase the brilliance and versatility of the ensemble, while Fisher Tull's inventive Variations on an Advent Hymn and Simon Wills's Prelude and Fugue explore its expressive and musical depth.

The holiday spirit shines through James Beckel's Christmas Fanfare, Ryan Meeboer's lively Hanukkah Swing, and seasonal favorites including Leroy Anderson's beloved A Christmas Festival, and Irving Berlin's White Christmas, arranged by Amherst resident and renowned composer, arranger, trombonist, and teacher Dave Sporny.

From the grandeur of opera to the excitement of traditional brass repertoire and the joyful sounds of the holidays, Music for a Festive Season promises an uplifting musical celebration for audiences of all ages.

Admission is free! Reserve your tickets through Bombyx.live. Donations are gratefully accepted to help defray expenses and support the Bombyx Brass Collective's educational programs, including collaborations with students in area public school music programs and performances for the wider community.
Join us for a festive celebration of music, community, and the magnificent sound of the Bombyx Brass!

events.title: Windborne
about: ++ THIS EVENT IS SOLD OUT ++ “The most exciting vocal group in a generation” -Songlines Windborne’s album “To Warm the Winter Hearth” smashed records and became the 5th most-backed album crowdfunder of all time! Now Windborne is bringing a full show of their favorite songs of the season to stages around the country!

A joyful and heartfelt celebration of song, Windborne’s lush vocals and unique arrangements bring light to a dark time, as they draw on midwinter music from traditional, classical, and folk from the US, British isles and beyond. Unique from their typical show, the holiday spirit is accentuated with added instrumentation, from banjos and guitars, to Lithuanian Kanklės, and Irish bodhran.

With Windborne as their guide across continents and centuries, audiences will be delighted by holiday stories, songs, and humor in an evening that is sure to become a holiday tradition for the whole family! Sing along with familiar favorites, enjoy new twists on old classics or sit back and enjoy discovering new favorites, but make sure you don’t miss Windborne’s Music of Midwinter!
"Sublime and superb... [Windborne] exhausts superlatives! Intelligent, witty, formally exquisite and brimful of energy." -RnR MAGAZINE Student and Card to Culture tickets available.

events.title: Lúnasa's Irish Solstice Celebration
events.detail: with Special Guest Singer Dave Curley
about: “The hottest Irish acoustic band on the planet” – The Irish Voice Named for an ancient Celtic harvest festival in honor of the Irish god Lugh, patron of the arts, Lúnasa is indeed a gathering of some of the top musical talents in Ireland. Its members have helped form the backbone of some of the greatest Irish groups of the decade.

Bassist Trevor Hutchinson was a key member of The Waterboys, and later he, with guitarist Donogh Hennessy, would form the dynamic rhythm section of The Sharon Shannon Band; Ed Boyd (Flook, Michael McGoldrick Band) has recently replaced Hennessy; Fiddler Sean Smyth is an All-Ireland champion who has played with Donal Lunny’s Coolfin; Kevin Crawford, considered to be among the finest flutists in Ireland played with the acclaimed traditional group Moving Cloud; and, piper Cillian Vallely of the famous Vallely artistic clan has performed with Riverdance and recently recorded with Bruce Springsteen. Folk Roots magazine has rightly termed them an “Irish music dream team.”

events.title: Light One Candle - “A Holiday A Cappella Experience”
about: Light One Candle 2026 is an afternoon of holiday harmony and captivating a cappella sound. Your host, Heart of the Valley Chorus, will perform alongside The Chill Harmonics, The Cider House Five and special guest singers to bring you the light and love of holiday favorites with opportunities for you to sing along if you wish. Singing, especially in groups, helps connect us with others in a way no other activity can. This event is intergenerational and it’s fun.
Let the light of our musical selections help spark powerful positive memories to lead you away from any darkness of the season.

Any proceeds from this concert enable Heart of the Valley Chorus to bring musical entertainment to underserved populations as the chorus seeks to expand opportunities to engage in meaningful musical outreach. This includes free concerts to nursing homes and the community as well as scholarships for youth to our young singers in harmony summer musical exploration program.
Would you like to sing on stage with us for this event? We are open to treble voices ages 9 and up. Click for a detailed flier. Click for the registration form (preferred deadline November 13).

events.title: We Celebrate the Light
about: Join High Five Books for a sparkling interfaith holiday celebration for families with beloved local author Heidi E.Y. Stemple, in loving memory of her mom, legendary author Jane Yolen.

On Sunday, December 13, 4:30-5:30pm, families are invited to BOMBYX Center for Arts & Equity to listen to Little Roots perform and hear Heidi read her and Jane’s co-written picture book WE CELEBRATE THE LIGHT, an empowering, informative, and inclusive holiday book for families of all traditions.
Now in its third year, this twinkly celebration takes on special meaning as we explore together how to honor loved ones who are no longer with us this holiday season.
High Five Books will have all of Jane and Heidi’s books for sale, and families are welcome to bring their own copies for signing.
Tickets are pay-what-you-will, and no one will be turned away for lack of funds.

events.title: Rickie Lee Jones
about: ++ Pre-sale: Thursday, August 13 @ 10am ET ++ ++ On-sale: Friday, August 14 @ 10am ET ++ Rickie Lee Jones is an American musician, storyteller, two-time Grammy winner and eight-time nominee who has been inspiring pop culture for decades, beginning with her star-making self-titled debut and the seminal Pirates. Named the “premiere song-stylist and songwriter of her generation” by The New Yorker and “The Duchess of Coolsville” by Time magazine, Jones released her Grammy-nominated album Pieces of Treasure in 2023, a reunion with Russ Titelman, who produced her first two records. Jones’ celebrated memoir Last Chance Texaco was named Book of the Year by MOJO and on Best of Year lists by NPR, Pitchfork, and many more. The Independent writes, “There has always been something defiant about Rickie Lee Jones... a voice from a dream, elusive yet familiar, transcendent, a messenger from another place.”

events.title: Paul Winter Consort | Matinee Concert
about: ++ The Matinee show is currently sold out but tickets to the Evening Concert are still available ++ In 1980, Paul Winter and the Consort were invited to be artists-in-residence at New York’s Cathedral of St. John the Divine. Paul Winter explains: “The dean had a personal mission to create a bridge between spirituality and ecology. He appreciated our music, but I think it was the ecological dimension of our repertoire that convinced him we could be part of the Cathedral. The premise of the invitation was entirely secular; it was not to have us play liturgical music. We could present any events we wanted, as long as we produced them ourselves.”

Since that time, the Winter Solstice Celebration has become a beloved annual tradition in New York City and for millions around the country, broadcast live on NPR. This year marks the fourth time that the Solstice Celebration has been held at Bombyx. “While we will not have all the dancers and theatrical effects that were possible in the world's largest Cathedral, we will have all the essence of our solstice music, and we will feature, as always, the beloved voice of Theresa Thomason, who has been the ‘star’ of our solstice celebrations for over 25 years.”

Join us for an intimate presentation of this magical tradition. The Consort will include vocalist Theresa Thomason, Eugene Friesen on cello, Bulgarian bassist Peter Slavov, Brazilian drummer Rogério Boccato, with Paul Winter on soprano sax.
Card to Culture tickets available. Limit two per purchaser.
NOTE: There is a limit of four tickets per purchaser. Premier Seating is presently SOLD OUT for the matinee performance.

events.title: Film Night! “Dreaming of a Jewish Christmas”
about: Film Night by Beit Ahavah! "Dreaming of a Jewish Christmas"

Set almost entirely in a Chinese restaurant, "Dreaming of a Jewish Christmas" is an offbeat, irreverent musical documentary that tells the story of a group of the Jewish songwriters, including Irving Berlin, Mel Tormé, Jay Livingston, Ray Evans, Gloria Shayne Baker and Johnny Marks, who wrote the soundtrack to Christianity’s most musical holiday. It’s an amazing tale of immigrant outsiders who became irreplaceable players in pop culture’s mainstream - a generation of songwriters who found in Christmas the perfect holiday in which to imagine a better world, and for at least one day a year, make us believe in it. Directed by Larry Weinstein.

events.title: Valley Jazz Voices Winter Concert
about: Take Route 66 to the moon and back! Travel with Valley Jazz Voices through the Great American Songbook. They got Cole Porter! They got Gershwin! They got Irving Berlin and Johnny Mercer! In 4-part harmony!

In the 50's and 60's, the US State Department "Jazz Ambassadors" program sponsored American jazz musicians touring all over the world. Why? Because jazz is America, with its invention and improvisation, its cooperation and competition, its swagger and its heartache. Jazz is a kind of multi-vocal democracy, and embodies what we claim are American values. That's soft power.

events.title: Ghost Ensemble: Evergreens
about: Ghost Ensemble creates experimental music that expands our perceptual horizons through shared immersive experience. Dissolving boundaries of genre, style, and scene, the ensemble collaborates widely with creators of contemporary chamber music, avant-garde jazz, and sound art, amplifying highly original musical voices to explore the most innovative and exciting music of our time. Since its 2012 inception, the ensemble has collaborated with a diverse range of composers who share a belief in music’s potential for individual and community transformation, including Sarah Davachi, Catherine Lamb, Miya Masaoka, Phill Niblock, Pauline Oliveros, and Yasunao Tone.

The new collective composition Evergreens is a collaboration between Ghost Ensemble, our Deep Listening workshop community, and Empowerment Through The Arts (ETTA). Alongside the musicians of Ghost Ensemble and ETTA, audience members with or without musical training may choose to engage as co-performers with provided text instructions and creative choices. Combining the roles of’ audience’, ‘performer’, and ‘composer’, Evergreens invites everyone present to engage with a novel musical situation, deepening our interconnected experience as musicians and as people.
With support from Northampton Arts Council and Massachusetts Cultural Council.

events.title: Secret Planet: Kayhan Kalhor
events.detail: A master of Persian classical music
about: Kayhan Kalhor is an internationally acclaimed virtuoso and the world’s leading player of the kamancheh, the Persian spike fiddle. He can hold a room spellbound with the instrument for an hour of unbroken improvisation. Through his many collaborations, he has been instrumental in popularizing Persian music in the West and remains a creative force in today’s global music scene. His performances of traditional Persian music and innovative cross-cultural projects have captivated audiences worldwide.

Born in Tehran with Kurdish ancestry, he began his musical studies at the age of seven under Master Ahmad Mohajer. A child prodigy, he was invited at the age of thirteen to work in the Iranian National Radio and Television Orchestra, where he performed for five years. With the Iranian Revolution under way and a new turmoil engulfing Iran, the seventeen-year-old walked out of the country carrying just a backpack and his kamancheh. He traveled more than 2,500 miles across Turkey, Romania, Yugoslavia and Italy, picking up farmwork until settling in Rome and pursuing a degree in classical music. Across several decades, he has constructed a musical resume that spans collaborations with the New York Philharmonic, Francis Ford Coppola, Toumani Diabaté, Yo-Yo Ma, Arooj Aftab, and more. After multiple nominations, he became the recipient of a Grammy in 2017.
He will be accompanied by the tombak player Behrouz Jamali for this performance at Bombyx. This concert will be fully seated; advance tickets are highly recommended.

events.title: Dura Mater in the Valley
events.detail: A Community Writing and Reading Marathon
about: Join us for Dura Mater in the Valley—a full day of durational writing, listening, and reading in community organized by poet Sara Jane Stoner and Northampton Poet Laureate Ari Banias.

Dura Mater in the Valley is a call to gather for a collective experiment in spontaneous, shared duration—a full day of writing, reading, and listening, alone and together with our desire to write and our need to feel our writing in relationship. After beginning with some collective decisions, intentions, and offerings, we will write for five hours with regular brief pauses, and an hour-long pause for lunch. Following our day of writing will be an evening marathon reading, open to the public, with time for each of us to share writing emerging from the day, along with a few reading slots for members of the community who join us. With generous space and time and attentiveness to our individual and collective needs, each of us can find and explore the postures and paths within writing we know and do not yet know we need—in proximity to others, maybe friends, maybe strangers, but all people who love writing and who have devoted themselves to being present for the unexpected possibilities held by the fullness of the day.
$10-$30 sliding scale fee. Advance registration required for the writing marathon. Spots are limited. Please contact Bombyx if cost is a barrier.

events.title: Jazz Shares: Jason Robinson
about: Blue Salience: For Yusef Lateef, is Jason Robinson’s epic tribute to the late Dr. Yusef Lateef, featuring an astonishing range of compositional, improvisatory, and sound approaches for his 17-piece Janus Orchestra. The concert features leading figures in the jazz and creative music scenes of New York, Boston, and Lateef’s long-time home of western Massachusetts.

It began as a simple idea with expansive implications. Where do the sound worlds of the legendary musician and scholar Dr. Yusef Lateef lead us today, and how might his sound worlds help us understand our current world? Composer, saxophonist, flutist, and scholar, Jason Robinson, long inspired by Lateef, began exploring these questions by returning to a consistent companion in his musical studies: Lateef's 1981 book, Repository of Scales and Melodic Patterns, an extensive study of musical theory and practice etudes. Like a humble thread called into service of an intricate weaving, Robinson discovered a series of inspiring miniature sounds and musical concepts drawn from Lateef’s book, transforming the ideas into rhizomorphic shapes, melodic passages, and harmonic and rhythmic ideas, ranging from small-scale motifs to large-scale forms. Raw stones polished into shimmering jewels through months of tumbling, Robinson’s music cuts to the deepest human emotions, bringing joy, longing, hope, and love into sound.

Thus was born Blue Salience: For Yusef Lateef, Robinson’s epic tribute to the late Dr. Yusef Lateef. 135 minutes, 13 pieces, an astonishing range of compositional, improvisatory, and sound approaches. Virtuosic performances by unique and leading figures in the jazz and creative music scenes of New York, Boston, and Lateef’s long-time home of western Massachusetts. Composed between 2021 and 2025, including during residencies at MacDowell and Yaddo, the striking, expansive sound worlds of Robinson’s compositions defy simple categorization, instead illustrating a mobility across genre boundaries and historical performance practices, ranging from jazz and modern classical music to irresistibly danceable grooves and heady abstraction. This is captivating, expansive music drawn from the vicissitudes of our modern moment.

events.title: Disney's Hexed
about: In Walt Disney Animation Studios' all-new magical coming-of-age saga, “Hexed,” an impulsive and unconventional teenage girl named Billie discovers secret magical abilities which, once unleashed, hurtle her into a spectacle-filled journey out of suburbia and into a vast witch realm called Hexe. Forced to team up with her cautious mother, Alice, they uncover family mysteries that could change the world of witches forever.
1 hr. 46 mins

events.title: Focker In-Law
about: This Thanksgiving, the Circle of Trust expands as Ben Stiller, Robert De Niro and Ariana Grande star in a hilarious new chapter in the blockbuster Meet the Parents franchise. Still operating as a helicopter parent to his adult kids, Greg Focker’s anxieties spiral out of control when his son brings home a formidable new girlfriend and reveals that he plans to propose.
1 hr. 46 mins

events.title: Hershey
about: Based on the life of Milton Hershey, founder of the iconic Hershey chocolate company. Milton's grit and determination to conquer the world of candy-making propel him from bankruptcy to monumental success, and the love of his life, Kitty, helps him build a legacy sweeter than any candy bar. But when Kitty falls ill, Milton’s wild optimism teeters on the edge of destruction, and she sparks an even bolder dream: to leave their fortune in the hands of America’s children in need.
1 hr. 48 mins

events.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping
about: From acclaimed director Francis Lawrence, THE HUNGER GAMES: SUNRISE ON THE REAPING follows sixteen-year-old Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) from District 12, beginning on the morning of the reaping for the 50th Annual Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell, the biggest Games yet with twice as many tributes.Set in the world of Panem 24 years before the events of The Hunger Games, the story follows Haymitch into the arena, where he forms an unlikely alliance with fellow tribute Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace) and joins a coalition determined to challenge the Capitol’s control under President Snow (Ralph Fiennes). As the competition unfolds, Haymitch risks everything to take down the Games from within the arena — setting in motion the rebellion that will change Panem forever.
2 hr. 38 mins

events.title: Ebenezer
about: This November, prepare to be ghosted. Johnny Depp is the deliciously unpleasant Ebenezer Scrooge in a thrilling reimagining of the most iconic ghost story of all time. On one unforgettable Christmas Eve, Ebenezer collides with his past, present, and future on a supernatural journey that will decide his ultimate fate. If you think you know his story, think again.
1 hr. 56 mins

events.title: Paper Tiger
about: In James Gray’s deeply felt and intense drama, two brothers become entangled in a scheme that turns out to be too good to be true. As they try to navigate their way through the dangerous world of the Russian mafia, family bonds begin to fray with life-altering consequences.
1 hr. 54 mins

events.title: Drummer Boy
about: As America’s fight for independence begins, a young drummer boy, an enslaved woman, and a divided family each search for freedom in a world built to deny it. With music carrying hope through battle and loss, Drummer Boy turns the Revolution into a deeply human story of faith, forgiveness, and the belief that no person is born to live in chains or be forgotten.
2 hr. 9 mins

events.title: I Play Rocky
about: The film is an electrifying true story about an unknown actor with an unshakable belief that he wasn’t just meant to write Rocky—he was meant to be Rocky Balboa. Told “no” at every turn, Sylvester Stallone bets everything on himself, holding the line on playing the lead against seemingly impossible odds. The result is the ultimate underdog story behind the ultimate underdog movie.
2 hr. 8 mins

events.title: Wild Horse Nine
about: “John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell are simply superb” (Deadline) as CIA agents facing a trust-testing mission from Santiago to Easter Island ahead of the 1973 coup in Chile. “See it with an audience… Wild Horse Nine is laugh out loud funny, brilliant and moving” (Variety).
1 hr. 58 mins

events.title: Wicker
about: An audacious comedic fable about sex, marriage, and the absurdities of social convention, WICKER tells the wholly original love story of an ostracized fisherwoman (Colman) who commissions a husband to be made by the local basketmaker (Dinklage). When her wicker husband (Skarsgård) proves more spectacular than she ever imagined, his soulful spirit and unique prowess awaken something inside her, setting off a wave of jealousy, fascination, and upheaval that threatens the very fabric of village life.
1 hr. 45 mins

events.title: Meet Me in St. Louis (1944)
about: The well-off Smith family has four beautiful daughters. Seventeen-year-old Esther has fallen in love with John, who has just moved in next door. He however, barely notices her at first. The family is shocked when Mr. Smith reveals that he has been transferred to a nice position in New York, which means that the family has to leave St. Louis and the 1903 St. Louis Fair.
1 hr. 53 mins

about: From acclaimed director Francis Lawrence, THE HUNGER GAMES: SUNRISE ON THE REAPING follows sixteen-year-old Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) from District 12, beginning on the morning of the reaping for the 50th Annual Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell, the biggest Games yet with twice as many tributes.Set in the world of Panem 24 years before the events of The Hunger Games, the story follows Haymitch into the arena, where he forms an unlikely alliance with fellow tribute Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace) and joins a coalition determined to challenge the Capitol’s control under President Snow (Ralph Fiennes). As the competition unfolds, Haymitch risks everything to take down the Games from within the arena — setting in motion the rebellion that will change Panem forever.
2 hr. 38 mins

events.title: Ebenezer
about: This November, prepare to be ghosted. Johnny Depp is the deliciously unpleasant Ebenezer Scrooge in a thrilling reimagining of the most iconic ghost story of all time. On one unforgettable Christmas Eve, Ebenezer collides with his past, present, and future on a supernatural journey that will decide his ultimate fate. If you think you know his story, think again.

events.title: Paper Tiger

events.title: I Play Rocky
about: The film is an electrifying true story about an unknown actor with an unshakable belief that he wasn’t just meant to write Rocky—he was meant to be Rocky Balboa. Told “no” at every turn, Sylvester Stallone bets everything on himself, holding the line on playing the lead against seemingly impossible odds. The result is the ultimate underdog story behind the ultimate underdog movie.

events.title: November 1963
about: Based on a true story, November 1963, directed by Academy Award®-winning filmmaker Roland Joffé and written by Nicolas Celozzi, the nephew of Chicago crime boss Sam Giancana, takes audiences inside the 48 hours surrounding the assassination of President John F. Kennedy and into the dark world of organized crime that may have been closer to the center of the story than history has revealed.Starring John Travolta, Robert Carlyle, Dermot Mulroney, Mandy Patinkin and Jefferson White, the film draws on first-hand accounts and insights from the family of Chicago crime boss Sam Giancana, and explores the alleged deal between Joe Kennedy and the Chicago Outfit that helped put JFK in the White House and the deadly betrayal that followed.With a secret plan, a second shooter waiting in the shadows, and a “patsy” positioned to take the fall, November 1963 reveals a side of the JFK assassination rarely seen before.One president. events.title: Swinging Steaks with Wishbone Zoe
about: Join us Friday, December 4th for the return of Boston’s own, Swinging Steaks, plus a killer opening set by local legend, Wishbone Zoe!

🎤 Boston’s own Swinging Steaks were doing “Americana” before it even had a name. Signed to the legendary Capricorn Records in the early ’90s, they broke out with Southside of the Sky — earning national praise, two AAA Top 10 singles, and stages alongside heavyweights like Los Lobos, The Band, John Fogerty, and Lynyrd Skynyrd.

With seven albums under their belt and decades of road-tested chemistry, the Steaks are still one of New England’s most beloved live acts. Expect killer harmonies, sharp songwriting, and that unmistakable mix of rockers, ballads, and mandolin-driven Americana that keeps fans coming back for more. A perfect night out for anyone who loves roots rock done right.

Wishbone Zoe is the multidisciplinary project of Western Massachusetts songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, animator, and visual artist Zosia Kochanski. Once described by Pitchfork as a “junkyard-rocker,” Kochanski’s music has moved freely between experimental folk, power pop, noisy rock, digital collage, and stripped-down acoustic songwriting, often incorporating homemade sounds, animation, and performance art. Recent releases like 2025’s Blue Distances and 2026’s Psyche’s Romp continue a catalog defined less by genre than by restless experimentation and a distinctly DIY sensibility.
🗓️ Friday, December 4th

events.title: Skyes Queer Curiosities: Return of the Childless Cat Ladies
about: Support Free Events

SEASON 4 FINALE: RETURN OF THE CHILDLESS CAT LADIES Riding the blue wave, the Return of the Childless Cat Ladies will descend upon Marigold Theater for our Season 4 finale. We’ll revisit the inquiry into the intersection of feminism, memes, and cats as explored in Skye Trivia Vol. 22 (October 2024), with new angles, new questions, and new possibilities for engagement from our community in the form of music, skits, stories, and more. Costumes to match the theme welcome, or simply wear blue, as we celebrate 4 years of Skye community. See you December 9!
Wednesday, December 9th · 84 Cottage St Easthampton Ma · Doors 7:00 PM · Show 7:30 PM · FREE!

We used to be called Skye’s Trivia Variety Show but we changed the name to reflect that it’s not pub quiz trivia night, even if a game of questions is involved. Each month we explore a different theme through music, skits, storytelling, games, or other activities as conducted or performed by those in attendance, our Skye community. But we also play a trivia game. Our goal isn’t to test you or incite cutthroat competition, but rather to playfully engage the theme. You’ll laugh, you might cry, and you’ll definitely learn something.
Teams of any size, play alone, play casually, or get into it. We’ll introduce you to some new people to play with if you’d like.

If you like to compete, Marigold gift cards of $50 and $25 for the top two scoring teams, and in Season 4, we have introduced the legacy Popcorn Noir Traveling Trivia Trophy from an alternate timeline. Winning team takes it home for the month, with license to adorn it as they see fit.

SKYE’S QUEER CURIOSITIES is a collaborative queer-run production and community event, written by Harper Doherty and hosted by Ivy Davida and Elana Rosičková. The three of us are a “system,” three distinct entities sharing one very non-binary, shapeshifted body (they/them). The show is named after our octopus Skye, in a nod to versatility and the focus on community outreach.
We welcome other collaborators anytime! Please JOIN OUR MAILING LIST for monthly updates and links to previous shows. or write skyetrivia@ Main Theater and Brattleboro Bar & Cafe WED NOV 25

events.title: The Moors
about: A hapless governess, a mysterious hero, scheming siblings, and the bleak setting of the windswept countryside: Jen Silverman’s The Moors has all the trapping of the best gothic yarns written by folks like the Brontë sisters. At once satire and homage to this source material, this dark and funny play also introduces us to two surprisingly literate animals and their star-crossed love. This richly weird set-up offers a unique lens to explore the things that motivate us: love, power, the search for connection.

Recommended for ages 16 and up due to adult situations, violence and gore, and references to sexual assault THE MOORS is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of Samuel French, Inc.

Recommended for ages 16 and up due to adult situations, violence and gore, and references to sexual assault THE MOORS is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of Samuel French, Inc.

events.title: Haley Kean - Passive Forms
about: December 5, 2026 - December 23, 2026 Art Walk and Artist reception: Saturday, December 5, 4-7pm Exhibition Statement: In Passive Forms, I explore the relationship between my hometown of Newtown CT, and the abandoned institution of Fairfield Hills. Drawing inspiration from Hokusai’s 36 Views of Mount Fuji Series, I created this body of work to illuminate the location that the people of Newtown live their daily lives around. The campus has been collectively reimagined as an active participant in the social ecology of Newtown; It has become a wayfinding device, a projection of self and community. In my work, I interpret space within Fairfield Hills, while emulating the visceral atmosphere of a place with layered identity. I do so through scale and detail within the etchings, juxtaposed with the spontaneous materiality of the plaster-casting process. I focus the project with large scale drawings that become abstracted vignettes of place and time on the site of Fairfield Hills.

Bio: Haley Kean is an artist based in Northampton, MA. They received their MFA in Printmaking from Ohio University, and BFA in Studio Art from Keene State College. Kean works with space, and narrative tools to visually interpret the radical compassion of the human experience, attachment, and grief.

events.title: Stories I Haven't Heard
about: Sung by Leo Harrison & Friends
December 11 · Pay it Forward 2026

After many years of feeling more comfortable behind the scenes, Leo is returning to performance as a means of voicing stories that have never been heard before. In pursuing ancestral connections, he feels drawn to imagine the lives of those who came before us, reclaim the songs that were stolen and lost, and maybe embellish the truth a little. Leo’s music conjures modern folktales, forgotten legends, and everything in between.

A gifted jazz vocalist, Leo Harrison (he/him) croons over syncopated bass lines, colorful keys, and hip hop beats with supreme ease. His cool, sophisticated musicality is reminiscent of Stevie Wonder and João Gilberto, not only in ingenuity but in his ability to convey complex ideas in deceptively palatable ways. This ability is more than a knack, it’s a means of survival. As an autistic trans man, Leo has to swim upstream, and his music is rife with Black American blues. Yet Leo perseveres, and his songs of love and everlasting comfort shine all the brighter.

Pay It Forward events are made possible by the Community Foundation of Western Mass, Massachusetts Cultural Council, Greenfield Savings Bank, Never Give Up, Greenfield Northampton Cooperative Bank, Tom Schiff Consulting, Tandem Bagel Company and Waugh Agency Insurance.

about: Scott Hsu, December 12 · Pay it Forward 2026

American Scott Hsu 許多藝 is releasing his new rock/pop album, 新生 Hsin Sheng, and celebrating with a release show! 新生 means “new life” or “rebirth.” Sung in Mandarin and English, the album explores love, hope, identity, and growing into something new.
Join Scott on Saturday, Dec 12 at CitySpace in Easthampton for a night of bilingual rock and pop. All ages are welcome, so bring the whole family!

Scott Hsu, is a Taiwanese-American rock/pop/electronica artist from Amherst Massachusetts. His songs are passionate and heartfelt, rooted in authenticity, gravitating toward themes of love, nostalgia, transformation, and redemption. With lyrics in English and Mandarin, he blends his cross-cultural heritage into his music to reflect his unique identity—global, hybrid, and personal. Scott’s latest singles include the dreamy Chinglish pop/punk song "陪你 / I Just Wanna Be With You" (2025) and the plucky pop Americana tune "You Got My Love" (2024). His discography includes his acoustic album Confessional EP (2025), and Cliffs EP (2024), which features the catchy synth rock single "Play"

events.title: Foes of a Minimum Wage Guard
about: Foes of a Minimum Wage Guard- A Solo Play, January 8 & 9 Pay it Forward Foes of a Minimum Wage Guard is an award-winning solo comedy-drama play in which a 68-year-old retail worker is suddenly reassigned to loss prevention without training and must protect a struggling department store—or risk losing his job. Performed by Ken Harris portraying 12 different characters, the play explores workplace pressure, resilience, and the search for dignity through humor, suspense, and heartfelt storytelling.

Ken Harris is a Springfield, Massachusetts-based playwright, actor, filmmaker, and solo performer whose work explores themes of resilience, social justice, and the experiences of everyday people. He is the creator and performer of Foes of a Minimum Wage Guard, an original one-man play portraying twelve characters and examining workplace discrimination, economic insecurity, and personal dignity through the story of an aging retail worker. Harris has performed the play throughout Massachusetts, Connecticut, and New York, including at the United Solo Theatre Festival in New York City. His work has been supported by the Springfield, Chicopee, and Agawam Cultural Councils, and he is a member of the Springfield Cultural Partnership Cohort. In 2026, Harris received the Mass Indie Spirit Award for his short film The Phantom Ruse. Through theater and film, he is committed to creating engaging, community-centered stories that inspire conversation, reflection, and connection.

events.title: Misty Blues
about: 2019 International Blues Challenge finalist, Misty Blues, is fronted by lead singer/band founder Gina Coleman. The band is based out of Berkshire County, Massachusetts playing original and traditional blues with hints of jazz, soul, funk and tent revival gospel since 1999. The band has recorded with Eric Gales, Charles Neville, Alexis P. Suter, Early Times, Kat Riggins, Candice Ivory and Joe Louis Walker, and opened for contemporary blues artists like Mike Zito, Albert Castiglia, Tab Benoit, James Montgomery, John Primer, Roomful Of Blues, Albert Cummings and Michael Powers. Misty Blues performs extensively throughout New England and has toured the continental U.S., Canada and the UK. The band has been nominated for a few Independent Blues Music Awards and their original recordings have broad international airplay. In 2024 the band had a song they released selected for use in a U.S. Presidential campaign ad.

In the summer of 1999 Gina Coleman was performing in the Williamstown Theatre Festival production of A Raisin In The Sun. That production featured the acting of Ruben Santiago Hudson, Viola Davis, Kimberly Elise and Gloria Foster. Coleman was cast as a gospel singer. Nearing the end of the show’s run, Ruben Santiago Hudson gave Coleman a cd collection entitled Men Are Like Streetcars. He told her that her voice was perfectly suited for the blues and urged her to take that next musical direction. Coleman heeded his advice, and after a quarter of a century, Misty Blues has stood the test of time.

events.title: David Dersham
about: “Marine” – an intriguing desciption of Dave Dersham's oeuvre, courtesy of New York based, anti-folk / improv-slam artist James O’Brien. Collectively, are songs of cautionary tales: submerging archipelagos; the unfolding eco-dystopia; and Samoan pigskin heroes. Dave spent his formative years in the Pioneer Valley of Western Massachusetts, meandered west, and eventually returned, despite mediocre snowpack, relentless rain – interspersed with draught – and unsettling occasions of smoke-infused humidity, the newest of new normals.

Dave completed his first CD, The Burn of Summer (2003) in Somerville, MA, engineered by Jabe Beyer, Tim Kelly, and Tom Eaton (Willam Ackerman). The crew synthesized the threads with elan, earning substantial airtime on Folk Radio’s WUMB (UMASS/Boston), WERS (Emerson College), and as a new artist finalist for Mountain Stage, a live, nationally syndicated radio production.

Gilding the Lilies (2011) was recorded by the kaleidoscopically-stringed lloyd Thayer of Watertown, MA, and Jared Fiske: djembe, electric/acoustic guitar, bass, keyboard. Corporate excess, mass-transit, and regrettable camping choices were some of the themes. The sophomore collection was well-received and distributed internationally.

A sly humorist, cultural critic, and melancholy optimist, Dave's third album, Another Interregnum (2024), addressed temporary out-of-body homelessness, relief from a burning planet, and working class bravado. The work was engineered by Andrew Atkin (13 Queen Studios) and recorded, mastered, and co-produced by Mark Alan Miller of Sonlab / Side Track Studio (Jay Mascus, Dar Williams).
Dave's 4th CD, Farce, will emerge in 2027.

events.title: TLI Presents: Berkshire Bach Portals—Working Musician—J.S. Bach Plays the Berkshires
events.detail: Studio E, Linde Center for Music and Learning
about: Presented in collaboration with Berkshire Bach Society, Working Musician—J.S. Bach Plays the Berkshires, is a short film about the evolving significance of Bach’s music in today's culture, told through the lens of Berkshire Bach and the way its performances come together. The film is by documentarian Anthony Rossello and features interviews with pianist Simone Dinnerstein, BBS Artistic Director Eugene Drucker, composer and music personality Bruce Adolphe, and critic Tim Page on what makes Bach’s music important for modern listeners. It includes telling anecdotes from Bach’s life and follows the preparations for the BBS signature series Bach at New Year’s featuring the six ‘Brandenburg’ Concertos. After the presentation, Eugene Drucker hosts a conversation with the filmmaker, the performers, and the audience.
BBS Portals is a quarterly series that explores creativity and the impact the music of J.S. Bach has had across artistic disciplines.

about: Step into the magical world of Cinderella, one of the most beloved fairytales of all time, brought to life in a dazzling Broadway-style ballet production filled with beauty, humor, romance, and unforgettable theatrical magic.

This enchanting production by the United European Ballet tells the timeless story of a kind and gentle young woman whose courage, grace, and belief in love lead her from a life of hardship to a royal ball and a dream come true. With expressive choreography, colorful characters, elegant storytelling, and the unforgettable romance of Cinderella and the Prince, this ballet is a perfect experience for audiences of all ages.

Set to the magnificent score of Sergei Prokofiev, one of the greatest composers of the 20th century, Cinderella combines classical ballet tradition with the charm and excitement of a grand theatrical fairytale. Audiences will enjoy elaborate hand-painted sets, exquisite costumes created by European designers, and a brilliant cast of international dancers who bring this beloved story to life with artistry, emotion, and grace.

Promoted by Classical Arts Entertainment under the leadership of Michael Art, this family-friendly production invites you to experience the magic of live theater at its finest. Bring your family, friends, loved ones, and children, and enjoy a beautiful evening filled with music, dance, laughter, romance, and wonder. Cinderella is more than a ballet. It’s a celebration of dreams, kindness, love, and the belief that magic can happen when the heart stays true.
Ballet in two acts with one intermission.
Suitable for ages 3 and up.

events.title: The Irish Tenors
about: For more than a quarter century, The Irish Tenors have thrilled audiences around the world with their unmistakable blend of soaring classical voices, Irish charm, and heartfelt storytelling. Since first joining voices in 1998, they have sold out iconic venues including Radio City Music Hall, Carnegie Hall, the Sydney Opera House, and The Hollywood Bowl, while becoming beloved PBS favorites through acclaimed specials such as Ellis Island. With millions of albums sold and a repertoire that effortlessly spans treasured Irish ballads, popular standards, and stirring contemporary favorites, The Irish Tenors have become one of the most successful Irish touring acts in the world.

This December, they return with The Irish Tenors: A Family Christmas, a holiday celebration that has become a cherished tradition for audiences across the country. Featuring beloved Christmas classics, inspirational seasonal favorites, and the rich harmonies that made their We Three Kings holiday album a perennial favorite, this festive program captures both the joy and reverence of the season. Expect an evening filled with warmth, laughter, nostalgia, and the unmistakable magic of holiday music shared with the people you love.

Led by the extraordinary voices of Anthony Kearns, Ronan Tynan, and Patrick Hyland, The Irish Tenors bring dazzling vocal power, emotional depth, and a touch of Irish sparkle to every performance. Whether delivering the spine-tingling beauty of “Danny Boy,” the festive exuberance of Christmas favorites, or uplifting songs that bring audiences to their feet, their concerts are unforgettable celebrations of music, memory, and togetherness. Gather the whole family and make this spectacular holiday event part of your Christmas tradition.

Join her quest in this heartwarming tale of longing and friendship, amidst the turning of winter into spring. Set to selections from three works by Peter Tchaikovsky: The Serenade for Strings, Symphony No. 1 in G-minor (Winter Reverie), and Incidental Music for the play, “The Snow Maiden,” and presented by students from the Amherst Ballet School and our volunteer company, this production is an excellent opportunity for young audience members to experience the magic of ballet for the first time. Several characters from the show will be available for photographs during intermission, and our director will give backstage tours to show how we bring a production together following each show.

events.title: Koffin Kats/Voo Doo Glow Skulls/The Raging Nathans
about: It’s been 20 years since Vic, Tommy, & E-Ball started The Koffin Kats in their parent’s basements and played for beer in local Detroit bars.

A psychobilly/punk band with influences ranging from The Damned to The Stray Cats, The Koffin Kats have covered a lot of ground,10 records, a few member changes, and close to 3,000 live shows from international touring.
The band has been continuously touring and releasing music. 2023 will see new music releases from the band while they celebrate 20 years of somehow keeping it all together for Rock and Roll.
You can keep up with Koffin Kats on all of the social media outlets. The band likes to keep it “old school” and suggests you check out their website at for all official information on news and tours.

Voodoo Glow Skulls were formed in 1988 by Eddie Casillas, Jorge Casillas, Jerry O’neill and Frank Casillas. After a few years of backyard party shows, cassette demos, 7” singles and first club gigs, they released their debut album “Who is, this is?” for Dr. Strange records in 1993, gaining the attention of Brett Gurewitz, owner of Epitaph records. The band then signed to Epitaph records and released four albums, starting in 1995 with “Firme”, their most successful album to date, then followed by “Baile de los Locos”, “Band Geek Mafia” and “Symbolic”.
The band began to tour worldwide with their first European tour in 1996 followed by Japan, Australia, Mexico, and South America.
The band has been featured on several of Epitaph's Punk-O-Rama releases and has had music featured in video games, TV and movies.

The song "Shoot the Moon" from the band's Firme album was used in the Pauly Shoremovie Bio-Dome and the band's version of "Used to Love Her" (originally written and recorded by Guns N' Roses) is featured in the Mr. & Mrs. Smith soundtrack.

The Raging Nathans are a punk rock band from Dayton, OH, known for their fast, emotional songs, brutally honest lyrics, and energetic live shows. Their sound pays homage to early Lookout, Epitaph, and Fat Wreck bands while forging their own identity, always putting the punk before the pop.

With catchy vocal melodies, sharp harmonies, and lyrics tackling relatable, sometimes uncomfortable topics, the band brings equal energy to basement shows and festival stages. Having toured extensively throughout the US, Canada, Europe, the UK, Mexico, and Central America, they've built their reputation the…

events.title: StageFright: A Tribute to The Last Watlz
about: STAGEFRIGHT brings a very special performance of The Last Waltz, which features an incredible collective of musicians reimagining the music, energy, and collaborative magic of The Last Waltz and The Band. These tribute performances have become beloved events at Union Pool in Brooklyn, NY and venues across the country. Expect timeless songs, rotating performers, a full horn section and an ode to the greatest concert film ever made.

events.title: FORAGER
about: FORAGER is a Brooklyn-based trio whose music augments contemporary indie rock with intricate guitar work, melismatic vocals, and curious, shapeshifting grooves. NPR's Bobby Carter called their music "buttery" and "complex," remarking, "where have you been all my life?!?" FORAGER has built their following on the strength of their live show, selling out venues in New York and throughout the U.S. Their sophomore album, Even a Child Can Cover the Sun with a Finger, ventures into rawer territory—whispered vocals over blaring sirens and distorted drums, singable psych-pop choruses that disintegrate into mayhem. The album captures the peeled-back intimacy of folk-singer-songwriters with the pulsating synchronicity that only comes from a band.

events.title: THEE SINSEERS: LOVE STORIES TOUR
about: Fronted by bandleader and son of East Los Angeles Joey Quiñones, Thee Sinseers have quietly chipped away at the sounds of R&B and soul since forming in 2019, bringing together their interpretation of music through an unmistakable modern lens. On their new Colemine Records release, 'Love Stories', one thing becomes abundantly clear: this is not an LP that explores a neat and tidy love story. It's interested in everything that comes before it, after it, and in spite of it. The band leaned into earthier instrumentation — standup bass, guitars run through amplifiers for a warmer sixties-adjacent tone. It's that cross-genre thinking that Quiñones sees as the record's defining quality. The band sought to capture the highs and lows of romantic relationships while expanding the frame to include the familial, the complicated, and the unresolved. Like an unsent love letter finally delivered, 'Love Stories' carries the weight of everything that was felt but never quite said.

events.title: LaMP
events.detail: ft. Russ Lawton, Scott Metzger, & Ray Paczkowski
about: Interstate jammers LaMP—featuring Russ Lawton (drums), Ray Paczkowski (keys), and Scott Metzger (guitar)—distill road-honed improv instincts as seen with their time with Trey Anastasio Band (TAB) and Joe Russo’s Almost Dead (JRAD) into taut, instrumental epics. The trio has hewn their own path behind their latest release, One Of Us, with kaleidoscopic interplay and club-shifting grooves, serving as a pure distillation of the LaMP sound and a mission statement of improvisational group-think.

events.title: Possessed By Paul James/Coleman Williams
about: After 20 plus years working within the realms of special education & advocacy work, Konrad Wert known as the band Possessed by Paul James, continues the balance with yet another upcoming album while in the classroom. Continuing to raise a family in Texas & working a 50 hr work week within public education, Wert has still been able to release 5 full length albums, two of which topped Bluegrass Billboard charts in 2013 & 2020. Possessed by Paul James’s upcoming 6th album, titled Fighting For Our Own Survival, set to release "sooner than later" highlights life’s passage with such tracks as See You On Sunday; recorded live here with WAF in Laramie, Wyoming & accompanied by Joe Macheret on fiddle.

As the fourth generation of the Williams family dynasty – preceded by Hank Williams, Hank Williams Jr., and Hank III – COLEMAN WILLIAMS is an independent musician with a very specific dream. To love and show pride of where he comes from without doing it just because he could.

Hailing from Nashville, Tennessee COLEMAN WILLIAMS strives to have everyone come out and get a little strange at his shows. Not as a gimmick, but because this world, if anything, is the same. He sings about his dog, things lost in life, and the others we gain because of it. Touring over the years, while fronting IV And The Strange Band, there were months at home where he began to experiment with somber song ideas and lighthearted stories, occasionally venturing alone onto the stage as well. To travel and learn, performing a bit more intimately with a different sound but still very much his own. His first recorded material arrived in the form of IV And The Strange Band’s album Southern Circus, released in 2022 on Megaforce Records, which was followed by the 2023-released Hang Dog LP which was produced by Shooter Jennings.

events.title: Jerry Wayne Longmire
about: Jerry Wayne Longmire is a veteran stand-up comic, original viral content creator, and well-known internet personality. A seasoned performer based out of Houston, Jerry performs for the troops overseas, delivers dynamic sets in intimate comedy club settings and theater venues alike, and produces 100% original, professional-grade social media content. His playful brand of storytelling and signature twang — reminiscent of an East Texas junkyard upbringing — effortlessly draws in audiences and captivates people worldwide.

With over 1.5 million followers across his social media platforms, you may recognize Jerry from viral series like the witty, sometimes frighteningly insightful Truck Astrology roast series, or the carefully crafted garage antics of Shoptalk. His videos across TikTok, Facebook, YouTube, and Instagram consistently reach nearly 300 million impressions across all platforms.

Jerry also works alongside Mattel's premier brand, Hot Wheels, as a recurring judge for their annual custom car competition, the Hot Wheels Legends Tour — where he draws on his unmatched knowledge of vehicles and impeccable taste to work directly with Hot Wheels designers and executives in selecting the custom build that will join the die-cast production lineup the following year.

Deep-cut fans love getting a glimpse of the "real Jerry" in his hilariously relatable and refreshingly vulnerable podcast, The Reckon Yard — a self-examination of his life, relationships, and Southern piney woods upbringing, told through the vehicles and junkyard lessons that shaped him. Now in its fourth season, The Reckon Yard has already landed a two-book deal for Season 1 — with full audio, TV, and film sub-rights.

At the end of the day, Jerry Wayne Longmire is the rare entertainer who can make a crowd of thousands feel like they're sitting around the fire with an old friend — and that's not something you can manufacture.

events.title: Whores.
about: Formed in 2010 in Atlanta, Georgia, WHORES. has established themselves as one of the most successful and motivated bands in the noise-rock genre today. Elements of Helmet, Melvins, and the Amphetamine Reptile roster can be heard throughout their catalog, but Whores. are no regurgitated throwback act. Through intense, cathartic live performances and the perfected aggressive tenacity present on their recordings, the band has gained a fervent following sure to do nothing but grow in the years to come TREE was formed in 1986 as a punk hardcore band in Westwood Massachusetts. The band played the club scene through the 80's and 90's in and around Boston and New England gaining popularity. Tree, always known to advocate for political and social justice, came to partner with MasCann ( and help spearhead the legalization movement in Massachusetts. Tree and Sam Black Church would be known to alternate headlining spots at the annual "Freedom Rally" on the Boston Commons, playing to extensive audiences of 100k+, and advocating for legalization. Tree's song "God Grows Grass" became the anthem for the movement.

Tree's recording "Downsizing the American Dream", recorded and engineered by Roy Z (Iron Maiden, Judas Priest), received extensive airplay and elevated the band to national status, facilitating the band to tour the country and be added to the Vans Warped Tour and the annual River Rave shows. The band took a hiatus in the late 2000's but reformed in 2021 and has been active since in performing, writing and recording new material. The band won the Boston Music Awards in 2025 for "Best Boston Hardcore Punk Band", and is releasing a new album "Missing in America" through Creep Records in November 2026.

Perennial is an art punk three-piece from New England. The band’s sound – built from the sharp minimalism of guitar, electric organ, and drums – is a kinetic collage of mod pop, 90s post-hardcore, post-bop jazz and 60s soul. The band’s ferocious live show – quick and electrifying – has already become the stuff of DIY legend, short bursts of manic energy with barely a moment to catch your breath: not to be missed. Perennial’s new album, Art History is available everywhere that chic modernist punk is sold

events.title: Day Drooler
about: Day Drooler is a five-piece indie folk rock band formed at Dartmouth.

Ever had a daydream that knocks you out? Now your mouth is open, you're drooling in public, you wake up, and everyone’s watching you. You are now one of us, welcome. We write jammy songs that start soft and get loud. They are a fly on the wall— telling stories about place and family, belonging, and not belonging.
This December (12-22), they are on tour through Brattleboro (Stone Church 12/13), Hanover (Sawtooth 12/15), Boston (O'Brien's 12/16 & The Lilypad 12/22), and NYC (Mercury Lounge 12/20).

events.title: The Sweetback Sisters- Oh What Fun!
events.detail: The 20th Anniversary of The Sweetback Sisters Country Christmas Sing Along Spectacular
about: Celebrating 20 Years!
Every family has its Christmas traditions. The cookies. The tree. The ornament that's been hanging on by a thread since 1987.
For thousands of people across the country, The Sweetback Sisters' Country Christmas Sing-Along Spectacular has become one of them.

For twenty years, audiences have gathered for an evening that feels less like a concert and more like the Christmas party everyone wishes they'd been invited to. One part country music revue, one part vintage holiday variety show, and one part joyful audience sing-along, the Spectacular is filled with classic carols, country Christmas favorites, forgotten seasonal gems, quirky originals, surprisingly consequential holiday trivia, improbable prizes, and enough laughter to keep winter at bay.

At the center of it all are Zara Bode and Emily Miller, two musicians whose extraordinary harmonies and effortless chemistry make everything look easy. Backed by their stellar band, they have spent two decades mastering a curious art: turning a room full of strangers into old friends before the final chorus.

There will be vintage finery, ribbon curls that defy both gravity and good judgment, songbooks for everyone, and just enough holiday pageantry to remind us that Christmas was never meant to be understated.

The magic isn't perfection—it's participation. It's the moment you realize you've stopped watching and started singing. It's the laugh you didn't know you needed, the harmony you didn't know you could find, and the feeling that, somehow, a roomful of strangers has become a gathering of old friends.
Come find out why audiences have been saying it for twenty years: It’s just not Christmas without The Sweetback Sisters!

events.title: The Attractors/Cousin Greg
about: Born in Brooklyn, based in Boston. The Attractors carry forward the legacy of the Brooklyn Attractors while uniting top players from both cities, delivering heavy Jamaican-influenced jazz, ska, and reggae with a modern edge.
Cousin Greg Vermont basement surf rockers

events.title: Shakedown CITI
about: Shakedown Citi is a fresh new force on the jam band scene, born in the heart of a Grateful Dead parking lot at Citi Field in 2023. When the band's members crossed paths on Shakedown Street, something clicked - and the music hasn't stopped since.

Rather than imitating the Dead, Shakedown Citi channels their spirit - creating spontaneous, soulful performances that feel alive, adventurous and totally in the moment. Each set is a journey, full of unexpected twists, deep grooves and musical conversation that pulls even the most skeptical listener into the vibe. Every Shakedown Citi show begins long before the first note. Each setlist is thoughtfully and meticulously crafted from the Dead repertoire, affiliated catalogs and beyond, balancing deep cuts and beloved anthems, rarities and reprises. No two nights are ever the same - each performance stands as a work of art on its own, alive in its moment, while also fitting into the larger patchwork of the repertoire.
It's not just a tribute - it's the Dead, reborn.

events.title: Boozer's Berfday
about: It’s a time honored holiday tradition where we gather around the alter an sing “F*CK YOU BOOZER”

events.title: Low Cut Connie
about: Adam Weiner is a rock & roll artist from Philadelphia who has released 7 studio albums under the name Low Cut Connie. Since forming in 2010, Low Cut Connie has earned a devoted fanbase that includes President Barack Obama, Sir Elton John and Bruce Springsteen. In 2024, he released the award-winning documentary film ART DEALERS. He has received acclaim from The New Yorker (“Pandemic Person of the Year”), Rolling Stone, NPR's Fresh Air and appeared on Late Night with Seth Meyers, The Late Show with Stephen Colbert’s #PlayAtHome Series and PBS Newshour. His writing has been published in SPIN, Billboard, and Talkhouse. On July 3, 2026, he will release his 8th studio album Livin in the USA.
Faux in Love is an indie surf-rock band from Southern Vermont. Equal parts modern and vintage, they invoke doo wop and punk in love songs that cut straight to your heart.

events.title: Lumos- The Beatles Candlelight Experience
about: Lumos brings you enchanting concert experiences paying homage to world famous artists. We’ve partnered with spectacular locations & churches across the UK & US to deliver a concert experience that is nothing short of magical ✨ 🌍A donation is made to a different charity each month!

events.title: Wolfman Jack Winter Residency
about: Primal Dead Sundays with Wolfman Jack returns January 3,10,17, & 24

events.title: Echoes of Floyd
about: Echoes of Floyd is a professional Pink Floyd tribute act that specializes in the accurate reproduction of the band’s legendary sound. Meticulous in detail, EoF faithfully reproduces the iconic songs and albums from Floyd’s vast catalog.

events.title: Night Zero
about: Night Zero - The night before the big event. The one you swear you’ll take it easy—but never do. Night Zero is the pre-party that becomes the main event, the night out you didn’t see coming but won’t soon forget. And now, it’s a band.

This cast of incredible artists brings together some of the jam scene’s most revered players for a raw, unscripted throwdown that blends rock, funk, jazz, and deep improvisation with nothing off-limits.

The core lineup is a one-of-a-kind fusion of styles and personalities, rarely seen together on one stage. Rob Compa (Dopapod), known for his mind-bending guitar work and precision improvisation. Gubb (Twiddle), whose unmistakable bass tone and groove drive every jam with grit and finesse. Adrian Tramontano (Kung Fu/Twiddle), a rhythmic powerhouse with jaw-dropping chops and relentless energy. Leon Campos (Dwight & Nicole), whose warm, soulful keys bring depth and color to every note.

These are players who don’t just complement each other—they push each other, unlocking something new every time they play. The kind of chemistry you can’t plan, only discover—when the right musicians collide at the right moment.
Night Zero —never planned, always unforgettable.

events.title: Vienna Teng
about: Some songs are the life of the party. Vienna Teng's are the back-porch conversation you still remember years later.

Her subversive choral piece "The Hymn of Acxiom” turns up in media literacy classes as well as drum corps shows (plus David Byrne’s blog, and the occasional flash mob choir in government buildings). The angst and effervescence in “Stray Italian Greyhound” has inspired anime music videos - and bridge-building political conversations. Americana-tinged "City Hall" has quietly become a queer anthem, a soundtrack for coming-out journeys. The electro-pop exhortations of “Level Up” have powered many a doctoral dissertation, first novel, and courageous battle with illness. “Harbor” is a beloved first dance at weddings and a graduation gift. “Lullabye For A Stormy Night” has been woven into countless bedtime rituals. These are songs that not only age well, but remain trusted friends throughout people’s lives.

It helps that Vienna's sound has never stood still. Her warm, delicate mezzo has drawn listeners since 2002, when her debut Waking Hour landed appearances on NPR's Weekend Edition, The Late Show with David Letterman, and the top of Amazon’s charts. But she’s built different worlds around that voice from album to album: the string-laced intimacy of Warm Strangers, the hushed jazz of Dreaming Through the Noise, the eclectically ambitious Inland Territory, the shimmering electronica of Aims. She’s world-built for other voices too, as composer for original stage musical The Fourth Messenger. You can hear how she’s metabolized influences like Paul Simon and Tori Amos, particularly their adventurousness and attention to songcraft. But Vienna Teng doesn't quite sound like anyone else.

Her perennial curiosity extends beyond music. In the 2010s, Vienna took a detour into graduate school and then professional work on climate solutions, turning in stints at the University of Michigan’s Erb Institute, consulting firm McKinsey’s sustainability practice, and environmental nonprofit Delterra. She also became a parent: first as a new addition to her partner’s family, then as a birth mother herself. Those years of carrying many truths at once led to her intricate 2024 release, We've Got You: two songs designed to be played simultaneously, as well as standing on their own.
Her love of multi-layering now informs her work with music fans as well as songwriting. In 2025,…

events.title: Charles McBee
about: Charles McBee is a NYC stand-up comedian, writer, and unapologetic 80s/'90s baby from Toledo, Ohio, serving up nostalgia with a side of truth. Whether he's breaking down the wild logic of gym class dodgeball or reminding you what it meant to record songs off the radio without your mom yelling in the background, Charles brings hilarious, heartfelt commentary about growing up in a pre-WiFi world straight to the stage. He’s made three national appearances on Gotham Comedy Live, was a standout on FOX’s Laughs and Punchline (Seasons 1 & 2), and has written for everything from VH1's Hip Hop Honors to the 2020 VMAs and the 2021 Golden Globes. He most recently served as Head Writer for Comedy Central’s Hell of a Week with Charlamagne Tha God, earning a Writers Guild Award nomination, and was a creative consultant on Nick Cannon’s Wild' N Out. Charles has also built a dedicated social media following with his no-holds-barred takes on pop culture, politics, and the beautiful chaos of growing up in the analog era. If you’ve ever eaten a microwave dinner on a folding tray table, feared getting caught in a game of freeze tag, or lived through dial-up internet, Charles has a joke for you. Come see why his fans keep coming back.
