events.title: The Meditations
about: One of the legends who has sculpted the Roots Rock sound with years of contributions to this music called Reggae.

As part of the foundation of reggae music, The Meditations have over forty years of producing, writing, arranging, and performing. They performed at the historical One Love Peace Concert in 1978 at the request of Bob Marley. Legends like Jimmy Cliff, Sly and Robbie, Philip Smart, Willie Lindo and Gregory Isaac are a few of the people that they’ve worked with. Their contributions have sculpted the sound of Roots Rock Reggae over the years, making The Meditations a fundamental and essential part of Reggae music. So therefore, when the other 2 original members were unable to continue the works, due to health and legal issues, Ansel had no choice but to keep the legacy alive. Joining forces with long time keyboard player / vocalist Laury Webb,who is also featured on The Good Of Man album and vocalist Daddylion Chandell, they’ve been touring as The Meditations for over 10 years. A new sound, a new feel, yet reminding true to the culture and origins of the band.

Touring together, their live performance have been praised by fans internationally, expanding their fanbase and introducing them to a new generation of music lovers. They’ve performed for massive crowds at venues like the Red Rock Amphitheater twice in seven years. And returning in 2013, to bring back Reggae On The River, a festival first opened by The Meditations and The Itals more then 29 years ago.

Criss crossing the United States year after year, embarking on journeys over waters to Africa in an attempt to quench the thirst for Meditations music worldwide. On January 29,2010 Ansel performed for exhilarated fans at The Parker Place(in Abidjan, Ivory Coast). This resulted in the culmination of a great live album, titled Ansel Meditations Live In Africa. This album captured an energetic performance from the veteran, sealing a monumental moment in time. Together, they’ve toured almost every year since joining forces, recently completing an autumn tour In November of 2017 and they started off 2018 with a bang, performing at the world famous B.B.KINGS in New York City on January 7th.
Without doubt, they’re loved and the thirst for their music is as strong as it always been. Roots Rock Reggae Lives!!!! The Meditations Forever…

events.title: Hans Williams
about: New Orleans-based singer-songwriter Hans Williams makes soulful, dreamy folk shaped by the people and places closest to him. His debut album, Songs for the Neighbors, was born in the backyard of his Bayou St. John home, where late-night jams and intimate shows regularly spill over fences and through open windows. Recorded largely live at the house with his longtime band and producer Phin Choukas (Noah Kahan), the record blends folk with touches of soul, funk, psychedelia, and country. At its heart, Songs for the Neighbors is about connection with friends, lovers, family, neighbors, and those no longer here. Warm, intimate, and deeply human, the album captures the feeling of people making music together and Williams’ belief that even the smallest act of reaching out can bring us closer. Now, Williams is excited to bring Songs for the Neighbors out of the backyard and onto the stage. To play these songs live, see familiar faces, meet new ones, and share the record with the people who have been listening along the way.
Hans Williams has partnered with PLUS1 so that $1 per ticket goes to supporting organizations working for equity, access, and dignity for all.

events.title: Bronwyn
about: For her third album, Rattlin’ Bones, Bronwyn, a Grammy-winning artist and two-time IBMA “Fiddle Player of the Year,” decided to purposely leave her comfort zone and dive headfirst into a new, unknown realm of musical possibility for the acclaimed artist — Songwriting. “If I’m going to be an artist and a front person, I’m going to need my own material that fits the live show,” Bronwyn says. “It definitely felt like a very steep learning curve, and it’s been very humbling, but the songwriting piece has been sort of the next step for what I want to do.” While her debut album, Fiddler’s Pastime (2020), was an instrumental offering showcasing Bronwyn’s fiddle skillset and prowess, it was the sophomore release, I Built A World (2024), that introduced the world to her singing style. And yet, with Rattlin’ Bones, it truly feels like Bronwyn has dug deep within to finally uncover and embrace her unique talents and sonic tones. “In a lot of ways, life has settled for me, where I’ve gotten married and it feels like certain pieces have fallen into place,” Bronwyn says. “And that’s given me space to stir up more chaos in my life by deciding to start my own band.” Backed by a whirlwind array of pickers, Bronwyn has elevated herself into the national spotlight of Americana, bluegrass and roots music as of late, which is why the urge to jump into the studio and capture this momentum and energy seemed like the perfect timing with Rattlin’ Bones. “I was just trying to follow my nose, basically,” Bronwyn says of the recording process. “What turns me on? What would I want to listen to? And I wanted to make a record that you’d want to turn up so loud, that it’d rattle your bones.” “All those moments underneath the clear blue sky/Even though you kept it going on the sly,” Bronwyn soars on “Johnny Ray.” “By the time we found our way across the track/Johnny Ray’d already been to hell and back.” This unrelenting force behind Rattlin’ Bones is due to Bronwyn hitting the road hard lately alongside her solo band, which includes mandolinist Tristan Scroggins, banjoist Frank Evans, bassist Larry Cook and guitarist Grant Dresnok. The ensemble is the cream of Nashville’s bluegrass crop, with their electrifying musical chemistry radiating a seamless sense of camaraderie and creativity. With her former group, Americana/bluegrass juggernaut Molly Tuttle & Golden Highway, dissolving amicably…

events.title: Suitcase Junket
about: Over the past twenty years, intriguingly single-minded songwriter/multi-instrumentalist Matt Lorenz has earned snowballing acclaim for his achingly poetic dark folk as The Suitcase Junket. A solitary artist with an organic yet ornate vision, his seventh album, To Go On is his most acutely profound yet. Created in the wake of losing his sister, singer-songwriter Kate Lorenz, it’s a tender, beautiful, and arrestingly moving record; an internal dialogue and conversation with the departed, enormously resonant to anyone who ever loved anyone. “Kate’s more on my mind than she ever would have been if she was alive, so there’s something sweet in that sadness,” Lorenz mulled from his family homestead in western Massachusetts. “When I’m singing and performing, I feel closer to her.”

Raised in rural Vermont and initially homeschooled, Lorenz and his older sister were unusually bonded even for siblings. Kate taught him to sing and was his first musical collaborator. Her little brother would scavenge and dissect old electronics, bikes, appliances, and watches, building instruments from the parts (he already played piano, violin, saxophone, and guitar). At Hampshire College in Amherst, Massachusetts Lorenz furthered these parallel passions, studying music and adaptive instrument design. After graduation and a year of busking in Europe, he returned to Amherst and formed the band Rusty Belle with his sister. Kate later became a folk-rock solo artist while Lorenz began The Suitcase Junket with a guitar rescued from a dumpster. The Suitcase Junket’s two hundred shows per year included treks across the US and Canada, European excursions, and a genre-straddling array of festivals including Hardly Strictly Bluegrass, Winnipeg Folk Festival, and California WorldFest. While Kate contributed vocals to all of Lorenz’s albums and often on stage, The Suitcase Junket was otherwise a truly solo affair in the studio, where he plays every instrument, and at shows, where he performs amidst a DIY cluster of contraptions including a suitcase bass drum, box-of-bones hi-hat, and a saw blade. The Suitcase Junket weds the sensibilities of early blues and rock ‘n’ roll, the improvisational spirit of jazz, and Lorenz’s love of Tom Waits to meticulous, cultured songcraft. Dubbed a “master of musical imagination” by NPR’s World Café Live and “astonishing” by WBUR Boston, Lorenz’s weathered,…

events.title: Dom Flemons
about: Dom Flemons is known as “The American Songster®" since his repertoire covers over one hundred years of American roots music. Flemons is a folk musician, black country artist, songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, music scholar, historian, actor, slam poet, record collector, curator, podcaster, cultural commentator, influencer, and the creator, host, and producer of the American Songster Radio Show on WSM in Nashville, TN. He is the Co-Founder and original member of the groundbreaking Carolina Chocolate Drops, the first ever black string band to win a GRAMMY Award. Over the past 25 years, he has received major awards, gained world-wide media recognition and has become one of the most influential and highly decorated voices in American roots music.
“Dom Flemons is one of the most accomplished American Folk Artists… few have pumped as much lifeblood into tradition as he has.” - MOJO Magazine

events.title: MARTIN SEXTON
about: Martin Sexton tours in support the 25th anniversary of Live Wide Open - the critically-acclaimed double vinyl live album. The show will include these fan-favorites as well as some new material and surprise covers.

“Mr. Sexton as an impassioned performer can bring women and men to tears when they see him live” —Wall Street Journal “The best live performer I’ve ever seen.” —John Mayer “Master of dynamics, reducing a room to silence with his blustering baritone, then teasing that silence with a fluttering falsetto."

events.title: VJC Big Band Celebrates its 22nd Year w/ Vocalist Charenée Wade
about: A gala dance to support the VJC’s Scholarship Fund!

The 18-piece Vermont Jazz Center is excited to celebrate 22 years performing big band jazz. For this concert, the VJC Big Band will celebrate the legacies of Sarah Vaughan and Ella Fitzgerald, and in a swing-dance performance featuring acclaimed vocalist Charenée Wade. All profits from this concert will subsidize VJC’s educational programs.

Vocalist Charenée Wade is renowned for her deep grooves and uncanny ability to bring energy and excitement to every performance. She was the first runner-up in the 2010 Thelonious Monk International Vocal Competition and has performed at venues and festivals around the world, including Jazz at Lincoln Center, The Apollo, and The Jazz Standard, Montreux Jazz Festival, Copenhagen Jazz Festival, Istanbul Jazz Festival, Spoleto Festival, Savannah Music Festival, Bern Jazz Festival, and Charlie Parker Jazz Festival. She currently serves on the faculty at the Aaron Copland School of Music, the Peabody Institute of Johns Hopkins University, and The Juilliard School.

The VJC Big Band is made up of area professional musicians who come together to enjoy the rewards of playing invigorating, challenging and historically significant repertoire while raising money for the VJC’s Scholarship Fund. Past headliners have included Carmen Bradford, Evan Arntzen, Alexis Cole, Amanda Carr, Houston Person, Dave Stryker, Samirah Evans, Rich Greenblatt, Mark Anagnostopulos, Rebecca (Bella) Holtz, Kevin Mahogany, Miles Griffith, Peter Eldridge, Wanda Houston and timbalero Eguie Castrillo.

events.title: 2026 Fall Semester Student Showcase
about: The Vermont Jazz Center (VJC) invites the community to celebrate the culmination of its fall semester at the Student Showcase on Saturday, December 5, from 12:00 PM (noon) to 5:00 PM. Over the course of the afternoon, ten ensembles will share the results of three months of study, rehearsal, and collaboration. Listeners can expect a mix of jazz standards, Latin jazz, samba percussion, vocal harmonies, improvisational forays and spirited tunes from the Blue Note era.

This performance highlights the depth of talent within the VJC’s education program, bringing together musicians of all ages and backgrounds. The event is free and open to the public; a suggested $5 donation supports the VJC Scholarship Fund.
This year’s Student Showcase will take place in conjunction with the Cotton Mill Open Studio & Holiday Sale.

events.title: David Sánchez
about: Grammy Award-winning saxophonist David Sanchez is widely recognized as one of the most distinguished saxophonists of his generation. Renowned for his unmistakable sound and remarkable command of the instrument, Sánchez brings together a deep understanding on jazz and Latin music with the rich traditions that shaped both genres. The result is a distinctive and compelling musical voice.

World-renowned jazz writer and critic Howard Reich has praised Sánchez’s artistry, noting that his “prowess on saxophone is matched by the intellectual depth of his concept and compositions.” Reich has also observed, “Technically, tonally and creatively, he seems to have it all.” Throughout his career, recordings including The Departure (1994), Sketches of Dreams (1995), Obsesión (1998), and Cultural Survival (2008) have demonstrated Sánchez’s ability to blend the language of jazz with the musical traditions of his native Puerto Rico and influences from across the Caribbean and Latin America.

Puerto Rican folkloric traditions are especially prominent throughout Sánchez’s discography. The influence of Bomba and plena can be heard on his debut album, The Departure (1994), and Street Scenes (1996). These traditions are further explored on Obsesión (1998) and Melaza (2000), both produced by acclaimed saxophonist Branford Marsalis, and on Travesía (2001), Sánchez’s first entirely self-produced recording.

events.title: Joe Lovano Joyous Encounter Quartet
about: Grammy-winning saxophonist, composer and producer Joe Lovano is fearless in finding new modes of artistic expression. With a Grammy Win for his 52nd Street Themes and 14 other nominations, he has won DownBeat Magazine’s Critics and Readers Polls countless times as Tenor Saxophonist, Musician of the Year, Jazz Album of the Year and Triple Crowns from DownBeat. He has also received numerous awards from Jazz Times and the Jazz Journalists Association for Tenor Saxophone, Album of the Year and Musician of the Year.

Born in Cleveland, Ohio, on December 29, 1952, he attended the famed Berklee College of Music in Boston, where years later he was awarded an Honorary Doctorate. Since 2001, he has held the Gary Burton Chair in Jazz Performance and has been a founding faculty member of the Global Jazz Institute at Berklee, directed by Danilo Pérez, since 2009. He is a guest lecturer at New York University’s Jazz Program, Juilliard and Manhattan School of Music, as well as a clinician at Universities around the globe.

From 1991 through 2016, Lovano released an unprecedented 25 records as a leader for the historic Blue Note Records. Joe Lovano Quartet: Classic! Live at Newport featuring Hank Jones was recorded in 2005 and released in 2016 to critical acclaim. In 2019, Lovano released his debut album as a bandleader on ECM Records, Trio Tapestry, with Marilyn Crispell and Carmen Castaldi. Over the next few years, Lovano saw the release of three additional ECM Records albums: ROMA, a collaboration with Enrico Rava; Arctic Riff, a special guest appearance with the Marcin Wasilewski Trio; and the sophomore release from Lovano’s Trio Tapestry, Garden of Expression. In 2021, Lovano released Other Worlds, his third album with Sound Prints, a quintet he co-leads with trumpeter Dave Douglas. The next year brought a collaboration with guitarist Jakob Bro, Once Around the Room: A Tribute to Paul Motian. In 2023, Lovano released his third Trio Tapestry recording entitled Our Daily Bread. In 2025, Lovano released Homage, a follow-up recording with the Marcin Wasilewski Trio. Most recently, Lovano released Paramount Quartet, with his ensemble of the same name featuring Julian Lage on guitar, Asante Santi Debriano on bass, and Will Calhoun on drums.
In addition, composer Mark Anthony Turnage wrote a Concerto for Saxophone and Chamber Orchestra for Joe called “A Man Descending,” which has…

about: Original and traditional music played on the Indian slide guitar alongside dynamic storytelling; fascinating tales from the lore of Hindustani music. Accompanied by Yousuf Kerai on tabla. An immersive performance experience in which the rich atmosphere of traditional ragas is woven into deftly told stories; guiding and uplifting the imagination of the audience while celebrating and continuing the rich tradition of Hindustani classical music.

“The late great George Harrison may have brought this musical spirit into the Western mainstream, but Veena takes Indian guitar right back to its roots, sharing the cathartic charm of North Indian ragas with global ears.”
This event is suitable for all ages.

events.title: Art Talk: Amy Beecher on Glotech Cantata
about: Amy Beecher discusses Glotech Cantata—a performance of movement, sound, and still images that interprets the dance between women and influencer marketing. Taking the Glotech LED facial mask as its motif, the work meditates upon our era of aspirational social media, where women are both the authors and the objects of images. This site-responsive performance uses “paintings”—large printed panels of still lifes, masks, and color abstractions—as both props and a movable set that frame, conceal, and cast color onto dancers, who pit improvised movements against stylized gestures and words.

Glotech Cantata was written, directed, and designed by Amy Beecher, with original choreography by Tess Dworman and sound design by Ryan Gamblin. It will be performed by Hilary Clark, Jessica Cook, and Mariana Valencia at the Campus at Marlboro Music on Sunday, December 13, at 12 p.m.
This project is funded in part by a Faculty Advancement Grant and a Research Assistance Grant from Emerson College, Boston, MA, and a Foundation for Contemporary Arts Emergency Grant.

events.title: Symposium: Immigrant Artists in Vermont
about: What has drawn immigrant artists to Vermont over the past two centuries? How has Vermont shaped their work, and how have these artists, in turn, shaped Vermont’s evolving cultural identity?

Through presentations, panel discussions, and audience Q&A, this symposium explores the experiences and contributions of immigrant artists in Vermont, from the stonecutters of Barre and Proctor and the founders of Marlboro Music to influential puppeteers and generations of landscape painters.

Four sessions on Saturday will be followed by an evening celebration featuring food and performances. A concluding panel on Sunday will bring together immigrant artists living and working in Vermont today to reflect on their experiences and look toward the future.
Image: Luigi Lucioni, Northern Lombardy (detail) (1938), oil on canvas, 14 x 24 inches. Collection of Shelburne Museum, bequest of Luigi Lucioni, 1988-27.3. Photography by Andy Duback.
This event is supported by a grant from the Vilcek Foundation.

events.title: Art Talk: Sara Jimenez & Sarah Freeman
about: Artist Sara Jimenez and curator Sarah Freeman discuss Jimenez’s installation the story never stops beginning or ending, exploring how textiles, ceramics, and collaged imagery bring together personal memory and histories of American colonization in the Philippines. Through layered landscapes and sculptural forms honoring Filipino women and non-binary individuals, Jimenez creates a space for reflection on history, remembrance, and care.

Sara Jimenez’s work gives form to histories that are often unseen or forgotten, exploring the shifting connections between ancestors, land, memory, and the present. Working across installation, sculpture, collage, and performance, she creates fantastical environments and otherworldly, biomorphic objects that transform these histories into visual metaphors.

Drawing from her kaleidoscopic connection to her genealogical roots in the Philippines, Southeast Asia, the Pacific, and the ancient United Kingdom, Jimenez considers how histories change as they move between places and generations, and how forms of memory can exist outside official records.

She draws on archival sources, historical narratives, family histories, and material culture, while also attending to the gaps and silences within official histories. She is interested in forms of resistance and survival that are often overlooked, including the preservation of knowledge, movement through landscapes, and the transmission of cultural memory.

Jimenez uses color, abstraction, and fantastical forms to complicate conventional ideas of monuments and memorials. Rather than presenting history as fixed or complete, her installations consider how objects can transform meaning and unearth history, while her sculptures create alternative ways of remembering. Her site-responsive projects extend this inquiry by responding to the particular histories, architectures, and landscapes of the places where they are made.

Sara Jimenez received her BA from the University of Toronto and her MFA from Parsons School of Design at The New School. Selected solo exhibitions include Rachel Uffner Gallery, Smack Mellon, and Morgan Lehman Gallery, all in New York City. Selected commissions include Cornell University in Ithaca, New York; Wave Hill in New York; and MadArt Studio in Seattle. events.title: Lydia Thomson: Of Fields and Feathers
about: Opening reception 12:00-2:00pm

Join Next Stage Arts for the opening reception of "Of Fields and Feathers," a new exhibition by Townshend artist Lydia Thomson, whose drawings and paintings take their subjects from the fields, hills, and roadsides surrounding her home on Deer Ridge Farm.

Working lately with natural inks, walnut and indigo, Thomson observes the Southern Vermont landscape as it shifts through the seasons, finding an unexpected loveliness in the weeds that grow along its edges. In works such as Roadside Swath #3 and Timothy, she pairs these inks with graphite to trace quiet, often overlooked corners of the land.

The exhibition also reflects a newer focus: birds. Thomson calls it “a late-in-life fascination with what has been around all along,” and pieces like Eastern Screech Owl #2 show her practice of finally paying attention, which for her is best done through drawing and painting.

An artist and teacher, Thomson has spent 35 years at River Gallery School in Brattleboro, a nonprofit art school founded 50 years ago on the belief that each of us has an inherent desire and ability to be creative. Since retiring as Artistic Director, she has continued teaching, grateful for the opportunity to work with people exploring their creativity.
Meet the artist, explore the exhibition, and enjoy light refreshments as we celebrate the opening of this attentive, seasonal collection.
This show will be on exhibit November 21-February 8. The Next Stage Gallery is open during events, and by appointment with the artist( or by contacting Next Stage at info@ or (802) 387-0102.

events.title: NXT Rockumentary Film Series
events.detail: A legendary band throws a circus, then hides it for nearly 30 years.
about: $8 suggested donation
Join us for the next installment of the NXT Rockumentary Film Series.

Filmed in December 1968, this British concert film brings together leading rock and blues musicians for a unique musical spectacle staged in a makeshift circus tent. Blending live performances with a playful, carnival-like atmosphere, the production features a diverse lineup of artists, ranging from energetic rock bands to blues performers and an experimental one-time supergroup. The event combines music, theatrical flair, and the spirit of the late 1960s counterculture.

Originally intended for television broadcast, the film was withheld from release because of concerns about the quality of the performances and the exhaustion of the musicians after an exceptionally long filming session. It also captures the final public appearance of one founding member of the featured band. Despite remaining unseen for decades, the film eventually received an official release in 1996, becoming a valuable record of an extraordinary moment in rock music history.
Due to licensing restrictions, we’re unable to publicly list the film title. To find out what’s screening, join our mailing list or contact us directly.

events.title: "An Irish Christmas" with John Doyle, Cathie Ryan and Mick McAuley
events.detail: A festive evening of Irish music, song, and story
about: $26 Advance / $30 At the Door / $10 Livestream John Doyle, Cathie Ryan, and Mick McAuley come together for “An Irish Christmas,” a festive celebration that brings three of Irish music’s most beloved performers to the stage in a program woven through with song and story — from cherished carols and traditional tunes and airs to newly composed songs for the season. A warm and joyful evening in the finest Irish tradition, “An Irish Christmas” is an annual holiday concert at Next Stage — a beautiful, thoughtful, and artful reflection on the season. Presented with Twilight Music.

John Doyle has established himself as one of the most versatile, creative, and prolific voices in folk and traditional Irish music. In 1994, he brought his brilliant and innovative guitar stylings to the nascent Irish super-group Solas, which soon took the folk and Celtic music worlds by storm. With Solas, John performed internationally to sold-out audiences and appeared on NBC’s “The Today Show,” “A Prairie Home Companion,” “Mountain Stage,” “E-Town,” and “World Cafe.” The group also received three NAIRD awards and a Grammy nomination. Since going out on his own, John has recorded as a solo artist and become a highly sought-after accompanist for the likes of Joan Baez, Eileen Ivers, Tim O’Brien, Linda Thompson, Seamus Egan, Alison Brown, and Kate Rusby.

Cathie Ryan is a natural fit for this holiday tour, having carved out a reputation for her own beloved Christmas performances over the years. A highly regarded singer, songwriter, performer, and educator, Cathie is a towering presence in traditional music circles on both sides of the Atlantic. She and John have been musical collaborators for decades: he has played guitar and contributed arrangements to three of her studio recordings, they have toured as a duo throughout Europe, and together they have penned songs that have earned a permanent place in the Irish music repertoire. Both are members of The Irish Music Masters and are featured on the PBS special “The Soul of Christmas.”

Mick McAuley, renowned melodeon player and longtime collaborator of John’s, co-wrote and recorded “This Christmas Time,” a holiday album the two released in 2024. That recording is the heart and soul of “An Irish Christmas,” and Mick is delighted to be bringing it to American audiences alongside two of his favorite musical partners.

events.title: Forever Simon & Garfunkel: Holiday Harmonies
events.detail: Celebrating the best selling duo in rock’n’roll history
about: $22 Advance / $26 Door / $10 Livestream With humor, soaring energy, charm, and laser precise harmony, Sean Altman & Jack Skuller lead the audience on a concert journey through Paul Simon and Art Garfunkel’s teenage roots, their early success as a groovy folk act, their global dominance as hit-makers, and even some of Paul Simon’s solo career. The Sound Of Silence, Bridge Over Troubled Water, Mrs. Robinson, I Am A Rock, The Boxer, Homeward Bound, Cecilia, Hazy Shade Of Winter, Feeling Groovy, Me & Julio Down by the Schoolyard, Kodachrome, and many more!

Award-winning singer-songwriters Sean Altman (Rockapella) & Jack Skuller (Songwriters Hall Of Fame Buddy Holly Prize) met on stage in 2010, when they were paired at a variety show to duet Mrs. Robinson. Jack had just celebrated his 14th birthday, and Sean had just celebrated his shiny new AARP card, but the audience found their December-January musical bromance and brotherly harmony to be enchanting and mesmerizing. The pair has toured as The Everly Set since 2016, celebrating the hits of The Everly Brothers. They formed Forever Simon & Garfunkel in 2020, and they tour both acts internationally.

Forever Simon & Garfunkel’s Holiday Harmonies features all of Paul & Art’s beloved hits PLUS numerous holiday gems sung in their classic two-part harmony by acclaimed singer-songwriters Sean Altman (Rockapella, Carmen Sandiego, The GrooveBarbers) and Jack Skuller (Songwriters Hall Of Fame “Buddy Holly Prize”).
Me & Julio Down by the Schoolyard Rudolph The Red-nosed Reindeer Run Run Rudolph

events.title: Sonido Mal Maiz
events.detail: Música es medicina: psychedelic Latin music to dance your worries away
about: $20 Advance / $24 At the Door / $10 Livestream Sonido Mal Maïz creates explosive psychedelic Latin music. The expansive creations of Sonido Mal Maiz emanate a passion for fire that ignites the heart and soul of music lovers. The band weaves together the rhythms and sounds of the Americas through spiritual improvisation and poetic storytelling of the myths and legends of Central America. Together we journey through the cosmovision of the past toward a creative collective future.
Described by the Seven Days as “Simmering with steamy dance vibes” Sonido Mal Maiz is the collaboration of Maiz Vargas Sandoval (vocal, bass)

Graham Lambert (guitar, vocals) Colin Henkel (drumset) Mike Hartigan (keys, vocals) who together weave a tapestry of creative expression to uplift the community. “Musica es medicina!” Sonido Mal Maiz invites the listener to shed oppression, worries and the struggles of daily life and to share in a ritual of rejuvenation and ecstasy within the music.

This play delves deep between the stanzas of everyone’s favorite Christmas carol, delighting audiences with quick-paced physical comedy, stage magic, and puppets, all performed by four actors. You’ve seen A Christmas Carol and The Nutcracker, this season why not try a new holiday treat, (Good) King Wenceslas, a winter play for winter people!

events.title: Joel Watson
about: 2026 Suzanne Fiol Curatorial Fellow Isabella Thorpe-Woods presents her culminating commission featuring artist Joel Watson. "Valediction," an expression used to say farewell at the end of a correspondence, brings her yearlong exploration of letters as a curatorial prompt to a close.

events.title: Leila Bordreuil: Numinosum
about: "Numinosum" closes ISSUE’s 2026 season and its celebration of the AIR program. Led by French cellist and composer Leila Bordreuil (2016 AIR), the work treats resonance itself as the primary instrument.

events.title: Hannah Ishizaki, Chiori Miyagawa, and Mark Campbell: A Thousand Generations
about: Composer Hannah Ishizaki is writing a one-act chamber opera in 11 scenes in collaboration with librettists Mark Campbell and Chiori Miyagawa for three vocalists, chamber ensemble, and electronics, based on the Japanese folk story, “Tsuru no Ongaeshi.” The story is split between a retelling of Tsuru no Ongaeshi (The Crane’s Gratitude) in 15th-century Japan and contemporary U.S. and Japan.

events.title: HANDEL + HENDRIX With Dither, R.B. Schlather, and Ruckus
about: Two radical innovators. Three centuries apart. One evening. Handel and Hendrix lived in adjacent homes in London's Mayfair district — separated by 250 years, divided by a single wall, now joined as the Handel Hendrix House museum. In honor of the museum's 25th anniversary, National Sawdust and Handel Hendrix House America present an evening that brings these two radical innovators into direct confrontation. Electric guitar quartet Dither open the evening with newly commissioned works that channel Hendrix's experimental language. Director R.B. Schlather and early music ensemble Ruckus then bring Handel's Deidamia — his final opera — to chamber scale in National Sawdust's intimate acoustic space.

events.title: LPR Presents: S. Carey
about: S. Carey is the moniker of Eau Claire, Wisconsin-based multi-instrumentalist, songwriter, and producer Sean Carey, commonly recognized as the drummer, backing vocalist, and second longest serving member of Bon Iver. Over the past decade and a half, Carey has fostered his flourishing solo career via themes of nature and sustainability, songwriting built from jazz beginnings, and heartfelt, emotive lyricism. His latest release, Watercress, adds to a discography of four full-length releases, two EPs, and countless collaborations, including Unbound with Bizhiki and Shadowlands with John Raymond.

events.title: Hildegard Commission Concert 2026
about: The Hildegard Commission Concert returns with groundbreaking premieres from our four winners, today’s most exciting rising composers—che buford, Līva Blūma, Fjóla Evans, and Maria-Eduarda Mendes Martin—along with works from our four brilliant finalists. The namesake of our commission, 12th-century mystic Hildegard von Bingen, used vivid, intricate miniature drawings in her prophetic books to bring complex spiritual visions to life. For this year’s commission, our winners have composed music that directly responds to a distinct illustration from Hildegard's codices. These historic images will be brought to life through dynamic animations and projections from a visionary visual designer, transforming the performance space into an interactive ecosystem of sight and sound. Step into a multi-sensory, immersive environment inspired by the extraordinary legacy of the 12th-century mystic Hildegard von Bingen.

events.title: inti figgis-vizueta’s Music for Transitions with Andrew Yee and Rothko String Quartet
about: Composer inti figgis-vizueta presents her 2026 debut record Music for Transitions, with a performance featuring GRAMMY Award-winning cellist Andrew Yee and the Germany-based Rothko String Quartet. Exploring Indigenous heritage and trans identity through playful, ecstatic soundscapes, the album exemplifies figgis-vizueta’s deep commitment to personal liberation through group improvisation. Recurring themes of land, wind, rivers, and cosmology are framed by constant musical transformation in what composer George Lewis calls “the dynamics of the decolonial.”

events.title: Caleb Wheeler Curtis & Jason Moran: "Incantation" Album Release Celebration
about: Saxophonist and multi-instrumentalist Caleb Wheeler Curtis and venerated pianist, artist, and MacArthur fellow Jason Moran celebrate the release of “Incantation” (Imani Records, 2026). Guided by their powerful and dynamic sounds and a shared fascination with musical ancestry, they explore space, time, and melody.

events.title: Creatine Price Presents The Drag Messiah
about: Lauded by the Huffington Post as "innovative" and "genre-defying" Hallelujah, gurl, the Drag Messiah 2026 is here! Creatine Price brings The Drag Messiah to National Sawdust for two nights of Handel’s Messiah like you’ve never seen before. The viral sensation is back and bigger than ever. Drag numbers, baroque opulence and glorious irreverence are what this holiday tradition are all about. In this queer reimagining of Handel’s Messiah, the grandeur of the music meets the wit and theatricality of drag. Joined by an ensemble of singers and instrumentalists, the operatic tenor and Drag Race France queen invites audiences into a celebration of community, self-expression, and the joy of making a beloved tradition your own.

events.title: National Sawdust Presents: Silkroad Up-Close featuring Yacouba Sissoko & Mike Block Duo and Maeve Gilchrist and Seamus Egan
about: Silkroad Up-Close offers a closer look at some of the extraordinary artists who make up the Silkroad Ensemble and at the ideas, traditions, and relationships that shape their work. Created as an intimate counterpart to Silkroad’s large-scale concert presentations, this flagship series gives Ensemble members the space to lead: inviting collaborators, tracing musical lineages, and developing programs rooted in their own creative lives. The result is a portrait of Silkroad from the inside, revealing not only the breadth of traditions represented within the Ensemble, but the curiosity and exchange that continually transform them.

events.title: Inside PROTOTYPE 2027—A Conversation with OperaWire
about: Join PROTOTYPE, National Sawdust, and OperaWire for a special festival preview celebrating the launch of the PROTOTYPE 2027 and the visionary artists, stories, and performances shaping this year’s lineup. Hosted at National Sawdust, this season preview will give audiences a first glimpse of the bold new works featured in this year’s festival. The evening will feature intimate performances and conversations with the composers, performers, and creative teams shaping the season’s most exciting projects—sharing the inspirations, processes, and stories behind their work.

events.title: Kyle Sanna: Everything Again Is New (Live Coding with Ensemble)
about: Composer, guitarist, and live coder Kyle Sanna presents the full premiere of Everything Again Is New, a set of algorithmic compositions for electronics and ensemble centered on themes of cyclical regeneration and renewal. Joined by Kinan Azmeh (clarinet, bass clarinet), Lily Holgate (violin), Nathan Koci (accordion), and Marika Hughes (cello), Sanna (guitar, electronics) will use code to reanimate recorded fragments of his own chamber orchestra work, all while projections show the generative process itself, as text becomes sound.

events.title: Emily Wells - Mirror Father - a workshop performance
about: For the past several years Emily Wells has been knocking on the door of an opera. Each year the door cracks open a little wider, the story gets louder, and the collaborators become clearer. This opera is a story about remaking the past in order to understand, and perhaps change, the future. It’s a conversation between a “mirror father” living the life he might have lived had he come out in the early 80s instead of living a closeted life, and his “phantom daughter” who he begins dreaming about. The two discover overlays: their queerness, their art, their relation to capital and its effects on community. At the center is each one's desire to have a child but choosing not to due to their fears of the end of the world, his AIDS, hers climate catastrophe.

events.title: BB Wisely
about: Hark! Behold: SLEDDING, the first full-length album from BB WISELY. You might listen to this album and think it sounds unusually seasoned for a debut, and you’d be dead on. That’s because the relationships between the three humans of this trio date back to the early 2000’s, when iPod’s had wheels and arguing about AI was something that happened in a Spielberg chat room. The musical and personal developments between Benjamin Lazar Davis, Bridget Kearney and Will Graefe have pushed forth since those days both in overlaps with each other and on their own circuitous career paths, but never has this trio acted as a unified whole until this very record: SLEDDING is here and it is one fully baked potato.
